1	# Cursor Cloud Agent provider: implementation plan
2	
3	Companion to [CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md](CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md) (the research) and the brief for a fresh implementation session. Every fact below was verified against the live API on 2026-10-13; the captures are checked in under `pkg/providers/cursorcloud/testdata/`.
4	
5	## Decisions already made
6	
7	| Decision | Choice |
8	| --- | --- |
9	| Scope | Full provider package `pkg/providers/cursorcloud`, registered and wired, so `sync` and `watch` produce markdown and cloud sync for cloud agents |
10	| Credentials | `CURSOR_API_KEY` in the environment, else `cursor_api_key` under `[providers]` in `specstory.toml`; environment wins |
11	| Watch | HTTP poller for `watch` and `run`; `sync` never polls. The provider guide assumes fsnotify, so every departure is logged in [PROVIDER-GUIDE-FEEDBACK.md](PROVIDER-GUIDE-FEEDBACK.md) instead of editing the guide |

13	| Fixtures | Real captures only. New cloud runs may be launched whenever useful; cost is tens of cents each. Repo `specstoryai/cloud-agent-test`, key in the macOS keychain item `cursor-api-key` |

15	
16	## 1. The native store is a remote API
17	
18	There is no file on disk. Cloud agent conversations exist only in Cursor's backend, so this provider is the first whose "native store" is an HTTP API. Everything the guide says about a store still applies, with the mirror standing in for the agent's directory.
19	
20	### 1.1 Endpoints used
21	
22	| Purpose | Call | Notes |
23	| --- | --- | --- |
24	| Probe for `Check` | `GET /v1/me` | `{apiKeyName, userId, userEmail, …}`; a Legacy-privacy-mode account answers agent calls with `400 validation_error` "Cloud agent is not supported in Privacy Mode (Legacy)" |
25	| Enumerate | `GET /v1/agents?limit=100&cursor=<nextCursor>` | `{items:[agent], nextCursor}` newest first; each `agent` has `id` (`bc-…`), `name`, `status` (`ACTIVE`/`IDLE`/`ARCHIVED`), `repos[].url` (`https://github.com/org/repo`), `url`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `latestRunId` |
26	| Agent detail | `GET /v1/agents/{id}` | same shape |
27	| Runs | `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs` | `{items:[run]}`; `run` has `id` (`run-…`), `status` (`CREATING`/`RUNNING`/`FINISHED`/`ERROR`/`CANCELLED`/`EXPIRED`), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, terminal-only `durationMs`, `result` (final assistant text), `git.branches[]{repoUrl, branch, prUrl?}` |
28	| Transcript | `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}/stream` with `Accept: text/event-stream` | SSE; replays in full for 24 h after the run ends (`x-cursor-stream-retention-seconds: 86400`), then `410 {"error":{"code":"stream_expired"}}`. Resumable with `Last-Event-ID` |
29	| Text fallback | `GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation` | `{id, messages:[{id, type: user_message\|assistant_message, text}]}` for the whole agent, all runs; ids are stable (`turn-N:step:M:assistant`, `turn-N:user`; the very first user message has a UUID id). Survives indefinitely |
30	| Usage | `GET /v1/agents/{id}/usage` | `totalUsage{inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheWriteTokens, cacheReadTokens, totalTokens}` and `cost.chargedCents`, per run too |
31	
32	Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Documented limit 20 requests per minute, no rate-limit headers; expect `429`. Fixtures: `testdata/fixture-run/` (a 5-step run, one of each basic tool) and `testdata/tool-enumeration/` (a 43-tool sweep with error results).
33	
34	### 1.2 Stream grammar
35	
36	Each SSE block is `id: <epochMillis>-<seq>` (absent on `status`), `event: <name>`, `data: <json>`. The `id` is the only timestamp source and must be used for message timestamps; never `time.Now()`.
37	
38	| Event | Parse | Meaning |
39	| --- | --- | --- |
40	| `status` | `{runId, status}` | first and last block of a run |
41	| `interaction_update` with `type: user-message-appended` | `userMessage.text` | the user prompt for this run; the only place it appears in the stream |
42	| `thinking` | `{text}` delta | concatenate consecutive deltas into one thinking part |
43	| `assistant` | `{text}` delta | concatenate consecutive deltas into one text part |
44	| `tool_call` | `{callId, name, status, args?, result?}` | several events per call; `running` may lack `args` while they stream; the last event for a `callId` wins; `result.success` on success, `result.error.error` string on failure; `run_terminal_cmd` also has `result.isBackground` |
45	| `result` | `{runId, status, text, durationMs, git}` | run finished; `text` duplicates the last assistant text, do not render twice |
46	| `done` | none | stream complete; its presence in a mirrored file marks the capture as whole |
47	| every other `interaction_update` type | ignore | `token-delta`, `text-delta` and `thinking-delta` duplicate the typed events; `step-*`, `tool-call-*`, `tool-requests-listed`, `partial-tool-call`, `thinking-completed`, `turn-ended` are lifecycle only. Name them in the kind switch as known-nothing-to-render |
48	
49	Segment order within a run is event order: thinking, text, tool calls, thinking, … One run is one exchange. Tool result pairing is by `callId` only.
50	
51	### 1.3 Tool inventory
52	
53	Names as recorded in `tool_call.name`, all observed in the fixtures. The model-facing names (`Shell`, `Read`, `Write`, …) differ; see `examples/tools.txt` for the mapping.
54	
55	| Name | Type | Input keys worth rendering | Result (`result.success`) |
56	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
57	| `run_terminal_cmd` | shell | `command`, `workingDirectory`, `description` (ignore `parsingResult`, `simpleCommands`, timeouts, ids) | `stdout`, `interleavedOutput`, `executionTime`; `result.isBackground` |
58	| `read_file` | read | `path` | `content`, `totalLines`, `readRange{startLine,endLine}` |
59	| `edit_file` | write | `path`, `streamContent` (full new content) | `diffString`, `linesAdded`, `linesRemoved`, `afterFullFileContent`, `message` |
60	| `delete_file` | write | `path` | `deletedFile`, `prevContent`, `fileSize` |
61	| `file_search` | search | `globPattern`, `targetDirectory` | `files[]`, `totalFiles`, `path` |
62	| `grep_search` | search | `pattern`, `path`, `caseInsensitive`, `multiline` | `workspaceResults{<root>:{content:{matches:[{file, matches:[{lineNumber, content}]}]}}}`, `outputMode` |
63	| `web_search` | search | `searchTerm` | `references[]{title, chunk}` (the chunk is a markdown link list) |
64	| `web_fetch` | read | `url` | `url`, `markdown` |
65	| `todo_write` | task | `todos[]{id, content, status}`, `merge` | `todos[]` with `TODO_STATUS_*`, `totalCount`, `wasMerge` |
66	| `mcp` | generic | `name`, `providerIdentifier`, `serverIdentifier`, `toolName` | `content[]{text:{text}}`, `structuredContent` |
67	| `get_mcp_tools` | generic | `server`, `toolName?` | `content` (may be a note that output went to a file), `outputFilePath` |
68	| `await` | generic | `blockUntilMs` | `complete{runtimeMs}` |
69	| `generate_image` | generic | `description`, `aspectRatio`, `filePath` | `filePath` |
70	| `write_canvas` / `read_canvas` | generic | `title`, `contents` / `canvasId` | `canvasId`, `title`, `url`, `source` |
71	| `pr_management` | generic | seen once in the research spike, args not captured | render generically |
72	
73	Failure shape, observed on `mcp` and `get_mcp_tools`: `result: {error: {error: "Invalid arguments", …}}`. The error branch takes priority for every tool. Anything not listed renders generically with type `unknown`.
74	
75	Strip the `toolCallId`, `conversationId` and `requestId` keys from rendered inputs; they are plumbing.
76	
77	## 2. Session model
78	
79	- One cloud agent is one session. `SessionID` is the `bc-…` id; `CreatedAt` is `agent.createdAt`; `Slug` and `Name` come from the first user prompt through `spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage` and `spi.GenerateReadableName`, preferring `agent.name` for `Name` when Cursor set one.
80	- One run is one exchange, in `createdAt` order. `ExchangeID` is the run id. `StartTime` is the first event id, `EndTime` the `result` event id. `Exchange.Metadata` carries `runId`, `status`, `durationMs`, `branch`, `prUrl`, `agentUrl`.
81	- Messages: the user prompt, then agent messages in segment order. Thinking and text are content parts on one agent message until a tool call interrupts; each tool call is its own agent message with `Tool{Name, Type, UseID: callId, Input, Output}`. Timestamps are the event ids as RFC 3339 UTC.
82	- `Model` stays empty; the API does not expose it. `ProviderInfo.Version` is `"unknown"`. `Usage` is per run in the usage endpoint, not per message, so leave it nil with a why-comment.
83	- When a run's stream is unavailable (`410`, or never captured) the exchange is built from the v0 conversation: the messages whose ids start with `turn-N:` for the run's turn index, with the first user message (UUID id) belonging to turn 0. Text only; record in `Exchange.Metadata` that it is `"source": "v0-conversation"`.
84	- `WorkspaceRoot` is the caller's project path. The VM path `/workspace` appears in every tool input; normalize path hints by replacing a leading `/workspace/` with the project path so `PathHints` point at real files.
85	- `RawData` is one JSON object built from the mirrored files of the same read: `{"agent": …, "runs": [{"run": …, "events": [...]}], "conversation": …, "usage": …}`.
86	- Debug output under `spi.GetDebugDir(id)`: `agent.json`, `conversation.json`, `usage.json`, and `run-<n>-<runId>.json` holding the run object and its events pretty-printed, numbered in run order; prune the provider's own stale files before writing.
87	
88	## 3. The mirror
89	
90	Path: `<project>/.specstory/cursorcloud/` by default, `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` from config (tilde-expanded) or `--user-data-dir cursorcloud:<path>` to override. Layout:
91	
92	```text
93	agents/<agentId>/agent.json              latest GET /v1/agents/{id}
94	agents/<agentId>/conversation.json       latest v0 conversation
95	agents/<agentId>/usage.json              latest usage
96	agents/<agentId>/runs/<runId>.json       the run object
97	agents/<agentId>/runs/<runId>.events.jsonl  one JSON object per SSE block: {"id","event","data"}
98	```
99	
100	Rules:
101	
102	- A run's events file is whole when its last record is the `done` event. A whole file for a terminal run is never re-fetched. A partial file for a terminal run is replaced by a full replay while the stream is still retained; after `410` it stays partial and the v0 fallback fills the exchange.
103	- Refresh is driven by `agent.updatedAt`: re-fetch runs, conversation and usage only when it advances past what `agent.json` holds. `sync` refreshes every agent matching the project before reading, within the rate budget.
104	- The mirror is the provider's native store for every read path: `GetAgentChatSessions`, `ListAgentChatSessions`, `ListAllAgentChatSessions` (whole mirror, every project), and `GetAgentChatSessionByPath` (`NativePath` is `agent.json`). `GlobalSessionRef.Fingerprint` is the sum of sizes and newest mtime across the agent directory, because one path does not change when a new run lands.
105	- Writes are atomic (write temp, rename) so a reader never sees a torn file. Lines in the events file are read with `spi.ReadRecordLine` and `spi.MaxRecordLineSize`; an oversized SSE block is skipped with a warning, not fatal.
106	- Open question for Sean: the project-local mirror holds unredacted raw transcripts and `.specstory/` is committed by convention. Decide whether the provider writes a `.gitignore` inside `.specstory/cursorcloud/`, or the docs tell users to ignore it, or it is committed knowingly.
107	
108	## 4. Project matching
109	
110	An agent belongs to a project when any `repos[].url` normalizes to the same string as the project's git origin. Normalization is the host-agnostic rule in `pkg/utils/project_identity.go` (`normalizeGitURL`: strip `.git`, `user@host:path` becomes `host/path`, strip `scheme://`). The origin is read from `.git/config`, walking up to the git root and following a `.git` file for worktrees (`resolveGitConfigPath`).
111	
112	Providers must not import `pkg/utils`, so move `normalizeGitURL`, `readOriginURL`, `findGitRoot` and `resolveGitConfigPath` into a new `pkg/spi/git_origin.go` as `spi.GitOriginURL(dir)` and `spi.NormalizeGitRemoteURL(url)`, with their tests, and have `pkg/utils` delegate. State this shared change in the PR. The v0 shapes give `github.com/org/repo` without a scheme; the v1 agent gives `https://github.com/org/repo`; both normalize identically.
113	
114	`OriginCwd` on global refs stays empty: the API knows the repo, not a directory. Log it as a guide/SPI gap (a ref could carry an origin URL so reindex can attribute by `git_id`).
115	
116	## 5. Provider behaviour per SPI method
117	
118	| Method | Behaviour |
119	| --- | --- |
120	| `Name` | `"Cursor Cloud Agent"`; registry id `cursorcloud`; `ProviderInfo.ID` `cursorcloud` |
121	| `Check(custom)` | No binary. Resolve the key (env, else config); none → failure `spi.CheckErrorNotFound` with guidance pointing at `https://cursor.com/dashboard/api` and both settings. Probe `GET /v1/me`; `401` → permission denied; other failure → unknown with the server message. Success: `Version` `"unknown"` (no version exists; see feedback doc), `Location` `https://api.cursor.com (key "<apiKeyName>")`. One `analytics.CheckAttempt` with `VersionFlag` `"GET /v1/me"` |
122	| `DetectAgent(path, help)` | True when a key is configured, the project has a git origin, and either the mirror holds an agent for that origin or one page of `GET /v1/agents` lists one. Guidance when false explains the key, the origin requirement, and that agents are matched by repository URL |
123	| `GetAgentChatSessions` | Refresh the mirror for matching agents, then build every matching session from the mirror; `progress` once per agent including failures |
124	| `GetAgentChatSession(path, id)` | Refresh that agent if it matches the project (a by-id lookup must still check membership), else `nil, nil` |
125	| `ListAgentChatSessions` | Mirror only, no network |
126	| `ExecAgentAndWatch` | No local process exists. Open `https://cursor.com/agents` with the configured `cursorcloud_cmd` (default: the OS opener, `open` / `xdg-open` / `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler`), print one line that the dashboard was opened, then watch until Ctrl-C exactly like `WatchAgent`. A resume id opens `https://cursor.com/agents/<id>` instead |
127	| `WatchAgent` | Poll `GET /v1/agents` every 60 s. Baseline on the first poll: mirror whatever is new but emit nothing. Afterwards an agent whose `updatedAt` advanced is refreshed and emitted; a run in `CREATING`/`RUNNING` gets a live SSE attach (one goroutine per run, bounded, `wg.Go`) that appends to the events file and emits the session on a 2 s debounce and once more when the run ends. Context per start; `Stop` joins every goroutine and drains before returning |
128	| `ReconstructSession`, `NativeSessionPath` | `spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported`; `SupportsReconstruction` false. Creating a cloud agent from a transcript would launch a paid run |
129	| `ListAllAgentChatSessions` | Walk the mirror; `OriginCwd` empty; `NativePath` `agent.json`; `Fingerprint` from the agent directory |
130	| `GetAgentChatSessionByPath` | Read the agent directory containing the given `agent.json` |
131	
132	Rate limiting: a client-side limiter of one request per 3 s (20 per minute) shared by every method, plus `429` and `5xx` backoff with `Retry-After`. HTTP timeouts: 30 s for JSON, none for the stream read but a per-read deadline of 90 s so a dead connection is noticed; a disconnected live stream reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`.
133	
134	## 6. Wiring
135	
136	- `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go`: `cursorcloud`.
137	- `pkg/config/config.go`: `cursorcloud_cmd` (commented, default opener), `cursor_api_key` (commented), `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` (commented, value `~/.specstory/cursorcloud`), the `ProvidersConfig` fields, the `GetProviderCmd` case, and rows in `config_test.go` so `TestProvidersConfigIsFullyWired` and `TestEveryRegisteredProviderHasACommandOverride` pass. The key and mirror settings are not commands; they reach the provider through two package-level setters the CLI calls at startup (`cursorcloud.SetAPIKey`, `cursorcloud.SetMirrorDir`), mirroring how `--user-data-dir` reaches `cursoride`. `ApplyUserDataDirOverrides` gains a `cursorcloud` case.
138	- `pkg/cmd/session_tui_browser.go`: colour `#4F8EF7` (a readable blue distinct from the grey used by the two local Cursor providers; adjust on both backgrounds).
139	- `main.go` and `pkg/cmd/resume.go`: the per-save line during `run` and the resume note are keyed to IDE ids; add `cursorcloud` to the `run` branch, since the dashboard, not a terminal process, is what the user is looking at.
140	- `README.md`, monorepo `../README.md`, `changelog.md` per the guide.
141	- `pkg/skills/agents.go`: no row; cloud agents read skills from the repo, not a local directory.
142	- `factory/latest-version`: there is no release channel for a hosted service; ship it printing the OpenAPI document's `info.version` from `https://cursor.com/docs-static/cloud-agents-openapi.yaml`, with the header explaining why `install` and `list-tools` do not exist.

147	
148	- Stream parser: block splitting, id-to-timestamp, delta concatenation, tool pairing where `running` lacks args, last-event-wins, error results, unknown events ignored, oversized block skipped.
149	- Session builder: both fixtures produce the expected exchange and message sequence; a golden `session-data.json` per fixture compared byte-for-byte; a second build changes no bytes.

153	- Mirror: refresh only when `updatedAt` advances; partial file replaced while retained, kept after `410`; atomic writes; `--user-data-dir` and config dir overrides.
154	- Watcher acceptance cases from the guide, mapped to polling: unchanged agents at startup emit nothing; an agent updated during the first poll is emitted on the second; a run that goes `RUNNING` to `FINISHED` emits during and at end; stop with nothing pending emits nothing and joins all goroutines.
155	- Debug output: unknown fields survive, `--debug-dir` honoured, stale `run-3-…` removed when a re-export has two runs, nothing written when the flag is off; `spi.SetDebugBaseDir(t.TempDir())` everywhere.

176	# Cursor Cloud Agents: why SpecStory misses them, and how to close the gap
177	
178	Research spike, 2026-10-06, in two phases: desk research (docs, forum, Cursor app bundle strings, local databases) followed by a hands-on spike that launched real cloud agents through the Cursor API against a throwaway repo. Covers the CLI (this repo) and the VS Code / Cursor extension (`specstory-monorepo`), which since February 2026 only wraps the CLI (`sync` then `watch`) and does no Cursor reading of its own.
179	
180	## 1. The problem in one paragraph
181	
182	Cursor Cloud Agents (formerly Background Agents) run the agent loop, inference and conversation state in Cursor's cloud. The transcript is stored server-side only, "kept indefinitely", and is never written to the user's machine. SpecStory's two Cursor providers only read local stores: `cursoride` reads `globalStorage/state.vscdb` (`composerData:` / `bubbleId:`) plus `workspaceStorage`, and `cursorcli` reads `~/.cursor/chats/<md5(cwd)>/<id>/store.db`. A cloud agent launched from cursor.com/agents, Slack, GitHub, Linear, the iOS app, the API, Automations, or the `&` prefix in the CLI never touches either store, so SpecStory never sees it. This is a data-location gap, not a parsing bug. The hands-on spike confirmed every part of this: two agents, three runs, and nothing SpecStory reads was written anywhere.
183	
184	## 2. What was verified
185	
186	### 2.1 Where cloud agent data lives
187	
188	| Surface | Where the transcript is | Reachable by SpecStory today? |
189	| --- | --- | --- |
190	| Cursor-hosted cloud VM | Cursor backend, encrypted per agent, indefinite retention (Enterprise can cap at 90 days). Inside the VM there is no transcript file at all (verified, see 2.3) | No |
191	| "My Machines" / Team Pool self-hosted workers | Still the Cursor backend. The worker only executes tool calls; docs say workers write no transcripts or chat files locally | No |
192	| Desktop IDE, cloud agent viewed in a window | No `composerData:` entry, no `bubbleId:` rows, no `~/.cursor/chats` store, no `agent-transcripts` file (verified). The IDE caches the agent list in `ItemTable` (`cloudAgentRepository.agents.<userId>`, `glass.cloudAgentProjects.v1`), protobuf state in an IndexedDB named `cloudAgentCache`, and a flattened, HTML-escaped text rendering in `conversation-search.db` (`source='cloud-cache'`) only for agents the user has actually opened | No for the providers; a lossy text copy exists only for viewed agents |
193	| "Move to Local" handoff | Becomes an ordinary local agent; the chat context is carried over. Not exercised in the spike (GUI only, and Cursor staff say the option only appears when a local agent for the same repo is already open) | Only after a manual handoff |
194	| Cursor mobile app | Device cache only | No |
195	
196	Sources: `cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent`, `/docs/cloud-agent/security`, `/docs/cloud-agent/self-hosted`, forum thread 165486 (Cursor staff: cloud sync "does not cover this local back and forth"), strings in `/Applications/Cursor.app` `workbench.desktop.main.js` (3.13.25), and the spike in section 6.
197	
198	Cursor also writes `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/<id>/<id>.jsonl` for local IDE and CLI agents. This is a flattened text-only transcript (no tool results). The cloud VM exports `AGENT_TRANSCRIPTS=/home/ubuntu/.cursor/projects/workspace/agent-transcripts`, but that directory is never created.
199	
200	An account on "Privacy Mode (Legacy)" cannot use cloud agents at all. Every v0 and v1 agents call returns `400 validation_error: "Cloud agent is not supported in Privacy Mode (Legacy)"`. Customers reporting missing cloud agent histories are therefore on standard Privacy Mode, whose conversations are stored server-side.
201	
202	### 2.2 The Cloud Agents REST API (`api.cursor.com`)
203	
204	Available on all plans in beta; cloud agent runs themselves need a paid plan. Auth is a user API key or a team service-account key (`crsr_…`), Basic or Bearer. Documented rate limit is 20 requests per minute; no rate limit headers are returned. All shapes below were observed live.
205	
206	| Need | v1 (current, public beta) | v0 (legacy, still live, no sunset date) |
207	| --- | --- | --- |
208	| Identity | `GET /v1/me` returns `apiKeyName`, `userId`, `userEmail`, names | `GET /v0/me` |
209	| List agents | `GET /v1/agents?limit&cursor&prUrl&includeArchived` returns `{items:[…], nextCursor}` sorted newest first; each item has `id` (`bc-…`), `name`, `status` (`ACTIVE` / `IDLE` / `ARCHIVED`), `repos[].url`, `url`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `latestRunId` | `GET /v0/agents` returns `{agents:[…]}` with `status`, `source{repository, ref}`, `target{branchName, url, prUrl}`, `linesAdded`, `filesChanged` |
210	| Runs | `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs[/{runId}]` with `status`, `durationMs`, `git.branches[]{repoUrl, branch, prUrl}`. `POST /v1/agents/{id}/runs` adds a follow-up turn to the same agent and VM | none |
211	| Full transcript | **No conversation endpoint.** `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}/stream` is SSE with `id:` lines (`<ms>-<seq>`) for `Last-Event-ID` resume. Events: `status`, `assistant` (text deltas), `thinking`, `tool_call` with `args` and `result` (including `stdout` of shell commands), `interaction_update` (step, token and tool lifecycle), `result` (`durationMs`, `git.branches`), `done`. **Retention is 24 hours** (`x-cursor-stream-retention-seconds: 86400`) and a finished run replays in full from the start within that window | `GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation` returns `{id, messages:[{id, type, text}]}` with `type` `user_message` / `assistant_message`. Text segments only: a run with 25 tool calls yielded 4 messages. Follow-up runs append to the same list. Message ids are stable across calls (`turn-0:step:22:assistant`, `turn-1:user`); the forum claim that they change did not reproduce |
212	| Webhooks | "coming" | `statusChange` on `FINISHED` / `ERROR` only, set at launch time, no transcript in payload |
213	| Usage | `GET /v1/agents/{id}/usage` returns per-run tokens and `cost.chargedCents` | none |
214	
215	Cost observed: the three spike runs were billed at 43, 23 and 12 cents, so a typical short cloud run costs tens of cents. A provider that only reads data costs nothing.
216	
217	### 2.3 Inside the cloud VM
218	
219	Verified by having the agents run probe commands and report the output:
220	
221	- Environment: `CURSOR_AGENT=1`, `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID=<bc-id>`, `CURSOR_REQUEST_ID`, `CURSOR_AGENT_SOCKET=/run/cursor/api.sock`. The metadata socket answers `agent/id`, `agent/name`, `agent/source` (`API`), `agent/runtime` (`managed`), `turn/id` (the run id), `workspace/repo-url`, `workspace/branch-name`.
222	- No transcript exists in the VM. `~/.cursor` holds only `agent-hooks`, `bin`, `projects/workspace/{canvases,terminals}` and `skills-cursor`. A filesystem-wide search for `*.jsonl` or `store.db` found nothing. `~/.cursor/hooks.json` is absent, so only repo hooks apply.
223	- Repo hooks from `.cursor/hooks.json` do fire: `afterShellExecution` (command and output), `postToolUse` (`tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_output`), `afterAgentResponse` (the full assistant `text`), and `stop` (`generation_id` is the run id). `sessionStart` never fires. Every payload has `transcript_path: null` and `user_email: null`, with `conversation_id` set to the agent id.
224	- `/tmp` and the working tree persist between runs of the same agent while it is `IDLE`, so a follow-up run sees files from the previous run.
225	
226	### 2.4 Official export paths
227	
228	The only official transcript export is the Enterprise OpenTelemetry "Conversation content" family, opt-in, which today covers Cloud Agents only, truncated to 32 KiB per message and 8 KiB per tool I/O side. The Admin and Analytics APIs expose usage metadata (`cloudAgentId`, `conversationId`) but never content. The web UI has no export or share for cloud sessions.
229	
230	## 3. What SpecStory has to work with
231	
232	- Every provider today is file-based. No provider imports `net/http`, there is no credential config, and the provider guide mandates fsnotify watchers. A cloud provider is a new pattern.
233	- Project identity is `git_id`, a hash of the normalized origin URL (`docs/PROJECT-IDENTITY.md`). The API's `repos[].url` normalizes the same way, so cloud agents can be attributed to the right project without any local cwd.
234	- Cloud sync (`pkg/cloud/sync.go`) already carries `rawData`, `sessionData`, `agentName`, and metadata; the Cloud Resume work means anything pushed as `SessionData` is browsable and resumable from any machine (`docs/CLOUD-RESUME.md`). Local markdown, however, is only produced by the CLI on the machine that captured the session.
235	- `specstory-sync` matches agents by substring (`agentName.includes(id)`); a new agent name containing "cursor" collides with the existing `cursor` entry and needs a distinct id.
236	
237	## 4. Options
238	
239	### A. New `cursorcloud` provider in the CLI, pulling from the Cursor API
240	
241	The user supplies a Cursor API key (`CURSOR_API_KEY` or `specstory.toml`). On `sync`, the provider lists agents, keeps those whose `repos[].url` matches the current project's origin, and for every run updated since the last sync replays the v1 stream, which within 24 hours of the run contains the complete structured transcript including tool arguments and outputs. Runs older than 24 hours fall back to the v0 conversation endpoint, which gives user and assistant text only. On `watch`, the provider polls the agent list and attaches to the stream of any active run. Markdown lands in `.specstory/history/` as usual and existing cloud sync pushes it.
242	
243	- Pros: covers every launch surface (web, Slack, GitHub, Linear, mobile, API). Reuses the whole provider → markdown → cloud pipeline. Works for local-only users with no SpecStory Cloud. Project attribution by repo URL is exact. Full fidelity for any run finished within the last day, which a daily `sync` or a running `watch` satisfies.
244	- Cons: new HTTP-provider pattern and credential handling. Runs more than a day old degrade to text only, and v0 may be sunset. v1 is beta and "may change". 20 rpm cap bounds polling. Requires the user to create an API key.
245	
246	### B. Server-side poller in SpecStory Cloud (`specstory-sync`)
247	
248	Users store a Cursor API key in SpecStory Cloud; a scheduled Worker lists agents and replays streams directly, always on.
249	
250	- Pros: never misses the 24 hour window, no CLI needed, and a team service-account key could cover a whole team.
251	- Cons: SpecStory Cloud holds third-party API keys (security and support burden). Only helps SpecStory Cloud customers. Local `.specstory/history/*.md` does not appear until the CLI pulls it down, which is new work (today only resume pulls cloud `SessionData`). Project mapping must happen server-side. Builds a second ingestion pipeline outside the CLI.
252	
253	### C. In-VM capture via repo hooks (`.cursor/hooks.json`)
254	
255	Ship a hook script that forwards `afterAgentResponse` and `postToolUse` payloads to SpecStory Cloud, or writes `.specstory/history/` inside the VM so it rides along on the agent's branch and PR. The spike confirmed these hooks fire in the VM and together carry the assistant text plus tool I/O, which is enough to render a session.
256	
257	- Pros: runs where the agent runs, independent of API retention windows.
258	- Cons: must be committed to every repo (or Enterprise-managed hooks). Writing history into the agent's branch changes the PR diff. Needs a SpecStory token as an environment secret. No `sessionStart` or transcript file, so the hook has to assemble the session itself from per-event payloads. Fragile across Cursor changes and invisible to users who did not set it up.
259	
260	### D. Opportunistic desktop capture (extend `cursoride`)
261	
262	Read the `cloud-cache` rows of `conversation-search.db` or the `cloudAgentCache` IndexedDB.
263	
264	- Pros: no API key.
265	- Cons: the spike showed this only exists for agents the user has opened in a window, and the search body is a flattened, HTML-escaped text blob with no structure. LevelDB/protobuf parsing is brittle. Misses most launch surfaces. Not a solution on its own.
266	
267	### E. Enterprise OpenTelemetry ingest
268	
269	Accept Cursor's OTLP conversation-content export into SpecStory Cloud.
270	
271	- Pros: official, admin-sanctioned, team-wide, no per-user keys.
272	- Cons: Enterprise only, opt-in by the Cursor admin, truncated content, cloud-only with the same local-markdown gap as B. Useful later for enterprise accounts, not a general fix.
273	
274	## 5. Recommendation
275	
276	Build **Option A** first, with **Option B as a follow-on** for SpecStory Cloud customers, and in parallel ask Cursor for a v1 conversation endpoint.
277	
278	Why A: it is the only option that works for every launch surface and every user tier while reusing the existing provider, markdown and cloud-sync pipeline, so both deliverables fall out of one piece of work. The user gets history on their local machine in the repo's `.specstory/history/`, and SpecStory Cloud receives it through the sync path already in place. The spike raised A's ceiling: the 24 hour stream replay means a daily `sync` captures the full structured transcript, tool output included, without needing to be online during the run. The text-only v0 fallback only matters for runs older than a day that were never synced. Attribution by repo URL is exact and needs no cwd guessing.
279	
280	Why B second rather than first: it closes the "machine off for more than a day" case but introduces key custody and a cloud-to-local pull that does not exist yet. Doing A first keeps B a thin addition rather than a parallel pipeline.
281	
282	Why not C or D: C requires per-repo setup and alters PR diffs; D only sees agents the user opened in the desktop app and yields lossy text. Neither can be the primary path. E is worth tracking for enterprise accounts.
283	
284	### Design notes for Option A
285	
286	- Provider id `cursorcloud`, display name "Cursor Cloud Agent", session id = the `bc-…` agent id, `OriginCwd` empty unless a local clone with a matching origin exists. Pick a cloud-side id that does not substring-match `cursor`.
287	- Polling: one `GET /v1/agents` per interval, per-agent work only when `updatedAt` advances. Stay well under 20 rpm.
288	- Transcript source per run: v1 stream replay (primary), v0 conversation (fallback after 24 hours). Treat `tool_call` events keyed by `callId` as the tool record; `assistant` and `thinking` deltas concatenate into the message; `interaction_update` can be ignored for rendering.
289	- Raw data: the captured SSE events plus the v0 conversation JSON, stored together so a later re-render can improve.
290	- Session metadata should carry `url`, branch and PR URL from `runs[].git.branches`, which is what users want to click, and `cost.chargedCents` from usage if we want to show it.
291	- `ExecAgentAndWatch` and `ReconstructSession` return unsupported for v1 of the provider; resume into a local agent still works through the generic `SessionData` path.
292	
293	## 6. Hands-on spike
294	
295	Method: a personal API key, a private throwaway repo `specstoryai/cloud-agent-test` connected to Cursor's GitHub app, and three runs launched with `POST /v1/agents` and `POST /v1/agents/{id}/runs`. The first agent probed the VM and committed a logging `.cursor/hooks.json` to its branch; the second started from that branch so the hooks were active, and a follow-up run read the hook log back. Each run was streamed live and re-fetched after completion, and the v0 conversation was fetched twice to compare ids. The first agent was then opened in the desktop app through `cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/background-agent?bcId=…` (which only works once a workspace window is open) and the local databases were diffed before and after. Total spend was under one dollar.
296	
297	Still unverified:
298	
299	- Whether "Move to Local" materialises a local composer. It needs a GUI session with a local agent open on the same repo.
300	- Whether a team service-account key lists other members' agents. The account used is personal, so no service-account key was available.
301
