package spi

import "log/slog"

// DispatchSession hands session to cb on its own goroutine, recovering from a
// panic so that one malformed session cannot take down a running watcher.
// label names the provider in the panic log.
//
// Delivery is fire-and-forget: a watcher that must wait for in-flight callbacks
// before shutting down needs its own WaitGroup around cb instead.
func DispatchSession(label string, cb func(*AgentChatSession), session *AgentChatSession) {
	if cb == nil || session == nil {
		return
	}
	go DeliverSession(label, cb, session)
}

// DeliverSession invokes a callback synchronously and contains consumer panics.
// Watchers with one worker use it to preserve ordering and join all saves before
// returning an agent's exit status.
func DeliverSession(label string, cb func(*AgentChatSession), session *AgentChatSession) {
	if cb == nil || session == nil {
		return
	}
	defer func() {
		if r := recover(); r != nil {
			slog.Error(label+": session callback panicked", "panic", r)
		}
	}()
	cb(session)
}
package spi

import (
	"os"
	slashpath "path"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

// Path hints operate on paths as RECORDED in session data, not host paths: a
// Windows machine renders sessions recorded on macOS/Linux/WSL and vice versa.
// Every operation here is therefore shape-based string algebra in
// forward-slash space — GOOS-dependent filepath helpers corrupt
// foreign-shaped paths (filepath.IsAbs("/project/…") is false on Windows, so
// nothing relativized; filepath.Join prepended cwd onto already-absolute
// recorded paths). Relativized hints come out forward-slashed, the markdown
// display convention on every platform.

// recordedAbs reports whether a slash-normalized recorded path is absolute in
// its own recorded shape: Unix-rooted (also covers slash-normalized UNC) or
// Windows drive-lettered.
func recordedAbs(p string) bool {
	if strings.HasPrefix(p, "/") {
		return true
	}
	return len(p) >= 3 && p[1] == ':' && p[2] == '/' &&
		('a' <= p[0]|0x20 && p[0]|0x20 <= 'z')
}

// NormalizePath converts absolute recorded paths to workspace-relative paths
// when they fall under workspaceRoot. This consolidates the identical
// normalization logic previously duplicated across all 5 providers.
func NormalizePath(path, workspaceRoot string) string {
	if workspaceRoot == "" {
		return path
	}

	p := strings.ReplaceAll(path, `\`, "/")
	root := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.ReplaceAll(workspaceRoot, `\`, "/"), "/")
	if root == "" || !recordedAbs(p) {
		return path
	}
	if p == root {
		return "."
	}
	// The "/" guard keeps a sibling with a shared name prefix (/project-api
	// under root /project) from being treated as inside the workspace.
	if strings.HasPrefix(p, root+"/") {
		return p[len(root)+1:]
	}

	return path
}

// expandTilde replaces a leading ~/ with the user's home directory.
// Returns the path unchanged if it doesn't start with ~/ or if the
// home directory can't be determined.
func expandTilde(path string) string {
	if !strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") {
		return path
	}

	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
	if err != nil {
		return path
	}

	return filepath.Join(home, path[2:])
}

```text
package musecode

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/analytics"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// Compile-time assertions that Provider satisfies the full spi.Provider
// contract plus the optional reindex capabilities.
var (
	_ spi.Provider           = (*Provider)(nil)
	_ spi.ProgressEnumerator = (*Provider)(nil)
	_ spi.PathSessionReader  = (*Provider)(nil)
)

// versionFlag is the flag Check probes the binary with, reported alongside the
// result so analytics can tell a flag change from a genuine failure.
const versionFlag = "--version"

type Provider struct{}

func NewProvider() *Provider {
	return &Provider{}
}

func (p *Provider) Name() string {
	return "Muse Code"
}

func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
	cmdName, _ := parseMuseCommand(customCommand)
	isCustom := customCommand != ""
	attempt := analytics.CheckAttempt{
		Provider:      "muse",
		CustomCommand: isCustom,
		CommandPath:   cmdName,
		VersionFlag:   versionFlag,
	}

	slog.Info("Check: verifying Muse Code installation", "command", cmdName, "customCommand", isCustom)

	resolvedPath, err := spi.LookPathForCheck(cmdName)
	if err != nil {
		errorType := spi.ClassifyCheckError(err)
		slog.Info("Check: binary lookup failed", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
		errorMessage := buildMuseCheckErrorMessage(errorType, cmdName, isCustom, "")
		analytics.TrackCheckFailure(attempt, errorType, err.Error(), "")
		return spi.CheckResult{
			Success:      false,
			ErrorType:    errorType,
			Location:     "",
			ErrorMessage: errorMessage,
		}
	}
	attempt.ResolvedPath = resolvedPath

	cmd := exec.Command(resolvedPath, versionFlag)
	var stdout bytes.Buffer
	var stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
	cmd.Stderr = &stderr

	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		errorType := spi.ClassifyCheckExecutionError(err)
		stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
		slog.Info("Check: version probe failed",
			"resolved", resolvedPath,
			"errorType", errorType,
			"error", err,
			"stderr", stderrOutput)
		errorMessage := buildMuseCheckErrorMessage(errorType, resolvedPath, isCustom, stderrOutput)
		analytics.TrackCheckFailure(attempt, errorType, err.Error(), stderrOutput)

		return spi.CheckResult{
			Success:      false,
			ErrorType:    errorType,
			Location:     resolvedPath,
			ErrorMessage: errorMessage,
		}
	}

	// A binary that runs but prints nothing still passes the check; report a
	// placeholder rather than an empty version so the result reads unambiguously.
	version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
	if version == "" {
		version = "unknown"
	}
	slog.Info("Check: succeeded", "resolved", resolvedPath, "version", version)
	analytics.TrackCheckSuccess(attempt, version)

	return spi.CheckResult{
		Success:  true,
		Version:  version,
		Location: resolvedPath,
	}
}

func buildMuseCheckErrorMessage(errorType string, museCmd string, isCustom bool, stderr string) string {
	var b strings.Builder

	switch errorType {
	case spi.CheckErrorNotFound:
		b.WriteString("Muse Code could not be found.\n\n")
		if isCustom {
			b.WriteString("• Verify the path you supplied actually points to the `muse` executable.\n")
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "• Provided command: %s\n", museCmd)
		} else {
			b.WriteString("• Install Muse Code and ensure `muse` is on your PATH.\n")
			b.WriteString("• Or pass a custom command via `specstory check muse -c \"path/to/muse\"`.\n")
		}
	case spi.CheckErrorPermissionDenied:
		b.WriteString("Muse Code exists but isn't executable.\n\n")
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "• Fix permissions: `chmod +x %s`\n", museCmd)
		b.WriteString("• Some package managers install the binary as root; run SpecStory with a path you can execute.\n")
	default:
		b.WriteString("`muse --version` failed.\n\n")
		if stderr != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Error output:\n%s\n\n", stderr)
		}
		b.WriteString("• Try running `muse --version` directly in your terminal.\n")
		b.WriteString("• If you upgraded recently, reinstall the CLI to refresh dependencies.\n")
	}

	return b.String()
}

// DetectAgent reports whether Muse Code has recorded any session for this
// project. The store is global, so this is a content question (does any
// transcript name this workspace root?) rather than a "does a directory exist"
// question.
func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, helpOutput bool) bool {
	sessions, err := findMuseSessions(projectPath)
	if err != nil {
		if helpOutput {
			fmt.Printf("Muse Code detection failed: %v\n", err)
		}
		return false
	}
	if len(sessions) > 0 {
		return true
	}

	if helpOutput {
		// Only the guidance below needs the store location; the detection
		// itself already resolved it inside findMuseSessions.
		sessionsRoot, rootErr := GetMuseSessionsDir()
		if rootErr != nil || sessionsRoot == "" {
			fmt.Println("No Muse Code sessions found.")
			fmt.Println("Start a Muse Code session in this project (e.g. `muse`) so a transcript is created.")
			return false
		}
		if _, statErr := os.Stat(sessionsRoot); statErr != nil {
			fmt.Printf("Muse Code sessions directory not found (%s).\n", sessionsRoot)
			fmt.Println("Run Muse Code once (e.g. `muse`) so the session store is created, then rerun this command.")
			return false
		}
		fmt.Printf("Muse Code sessions exist under %s but none record this project as their workspace root.\n", sessionsRoot)
		fmt.Println("Start a Muse Code session from this directory so the provider can pick it up.")
	}
	return false
}

func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	projectPath, err := defaultProjectPath(projectPath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	files, err := findMuseSessions(projectPath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	var result []spi.AgentChatSession
	for i, file := range files {
		if chatSession := parseAndConvert(file.Path, projectPath, debugRaw); chatSession != nil {
			result = append(result, *chatSession)
		}

		// Report progress after each session
		if progress != nil {
			progress(i+1, len(files))
		}
	}
	return result, nil
}

func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath string, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	projectPath, err := defaultProjectPath(projectPath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	// The store is keyed by session id (the id IS the directory name), so a
	// glob resolves the path without reading any transcript.
	//
	// The id alone does not establish ownership, though: the store is global, so
	// the glob will just as happily find another project's session. Confirm the
	// transcript names this project before converting it — conversion stamps the
	// requested project onto the result, so returning an unchecked match would
	// file one project's conversation under another. The scan below applies the
	// same rule via findMuseSessions.
	directPath, err := findMuseSessionPathByID(sessionID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if directPath != "" && sessionFileBelongsToProject(directPath, projectPath) {
		if chatSession := parseAndConvert(directPath, projectPath, debugRaw); chatSession != nil {
			return chatSession, nil
		}
	}

	// Fall back to a scan: the id may name a session recorded under a layout
	// the glob does not cover.
	files, err := findMuseSessions(projectPath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	for _, file := range files {
		if file.SessionID == sessionID {
			return parseAndConvert(file.Path, projectPath, debugRaw), nil
		}
	}

	return nil, nil
}

// GetAgentChatSessionByPath parses a single session directly from its known
// native file path, skipping by-id discovery. Used by reindex (which already
// holds NativePath from enumeration) to keep resolving N sessions O(N).
func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath string, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	session, err := ParseSessionFile(nativePath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(session.Events) == 0 {
		return nil, nil
	}
	return convertToAgentChatSession(session, originCwd, debugRaw), nil
}
```

```text
package spi

import (
	"errors"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"
	"strings"
)

// LookPathForCheck resolves a probe executable without hiding permission errors
// behind Unix LookPath's final ErrNotFound when no PATH candidate is executable.
// A runnable later candidate still wins, exactly as it does for exec.LookPath.
func LookPathForCheck(command string) (string, error) {
	path, err := exec.LookPath(command)
	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" || !errors.Is(err, exec.ErrNotFound) || strings.ContainsRune(command, '/') {
		return path, err
	}
	for _, dir := range filepath.SplitList(os.Getenv("PATH")) {
		if dir == "" {
			dir = "."
		}
		candidate := filepath.Join(dir, command)
		// Ensure a relative PATH entry is treated as a path, not another PATH lookup.
		candidate, absErr := filepath.Abs(candidate)
		if absErr != nil {
			continue
		}
		if _, candidateErr := exec.LookPath(candidate); candidateErr != nil && ClassifyCheckError(candidateErr) != CheckErrorNotFound {
			return "", candidateErr
		}
	}
	return path, err
}

// Error types reported by ClassifyCheckError. They are also the values a
// provider reports to analytics, so they are stable identifiers rather than
// display text.
const (
	CheckErrorNotFound         = "not_found"         // the agent binary or IDE storage was not found
	CheckErrorPermissionDenied = "permission_denied" // access to the binary or IDE storage is denied
	CheckErrorUnknown          = "unknown"           // the probe failed for a reason worth reading error_message for

	// CheckErrorNoOutput is reported by a provider directly rather than by
	// ClassifyCheckError: the probe exited cleanly but printed no version, which
	// is a successful run producing an unusable result, not an error to classify.
	CheckErrorNoOutput = "no_output"

	// CheckErrorUnexpectedOutput means the probe output did not identify the expected agent.
	CheckErrorUnexpectedOutput = "unexpected_output"
)

// ClassifyCheckError buckets a lookup or storage failure during Provider.Check
// into one of the CheckError* types, so that the caller can
// choose remediation advice and report a consistent error type to analytics.
// A nil error classifies as "" — nothing failed.
//
// CheckErrorUnknown is the residual: it means the failure could not be
// attributed to a missing binary or a permission problem, so error_message is
// the only thing that explains it. Callers may also treat it as "not fatal,
// worth retrying differently" — codexcli uses it that way to decide whether to
// try another version flag.
func ClassifyCheckError(err error) string {
	switch {
	case err == nil:
		return ""
	case errors.Is(err, exec.ErrNotFound), errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist):
		return CheckErrorNotFound
	case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
		return CheckErrorPermissionDenied
	default:
		return CheckErrorUnknown
	}
}

// ClassifyCheckExecutionError classifies a probe failure after the executable was
// found. ENOENT here can mean a broken interpreter or dynamic loader, so it must
// not make an installed but broken agent look like an absent optional agent.
func ClassifyCheckExecutionError(err error) string {
	errorType := ClassifyCheckError(err)
	if errorType == CheckErrorNotFound {
		return CheckErrorUnknown
	}
	return errorType
}
```

```text
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/qwencode"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// Registry manages all registered providers
type Registry struct {
	providers         map[string]spi.Provider // key is the provider ID (e.g., "claude", "cursor")
	mu                sync.RWMutex
	initialized       bool
	providerListCache string    // Cached formatted provider list string
	providerListOnce  sync.Once // Ensures provider list is built only once
}

// Global registry instance
var (
	registry = &Registry{
		providers: make(map[string]spi.Provider),
	}
	once sync.Once
)

// ensureInitialized makes sure providers are registered
func (r *Registry) ensureInitialized() {
	once.Do(func() {
		r.registerAll()
	})
}

// registerAll registers all known providers.
// This is the ONLY place that needs to be updated when adding new providers.
func (r *Registry) registerAll() {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()

	if r.initialized {
		slog.Debug("Provider registry already initialized, skipping registration")
		return
	}

	slog.Debug("Initializing provider registry")

	// Register providers with simple IDs
	// Each provider directly implements the spi.Provider interface
	claudeProvider := claudecode.NewProvider()
	r.providers["claude"] = claudeProvider
	slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", "claude", "name", claudeProvider.Name())

	cursorProvider := cursorcli.NewProvider()
	r.providers["cursor"] = cursorProvider
	slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", "cursor", "name", cursorProvider.Name())

	codexProvider := codexcli.NewProvider()
	r.providers["codex"] = codexProvider
	slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", "codex", "name", codexProvider.Name())
```

```sh
# Captures a two-run cloud agent with deliberate tool failures, plus a 410 from an

H=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY")
c() { curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 "${H[@]}" "$@"; }

wait_run() { # agent run -> waits until terminal
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do
    s=$(c "$API/v1/agents/$1/runs/$2" | python3 -I -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("status",""))')
    echo "run $2 status $s" >&2
    case "$s" in FINISHED|ERROR|CANCELLED|EXPIRED) return 0;; esac
    sleep 15
  done
}
```

```go
package spi

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
)

// Git origin helpers shared by project identity (pkg/utils) and by providers
// that match sessions to a project by repository rather than by directory. They
// live here because providers may not import pkg/utils, and a provider that
// normalized URLs its own way would attribute sessions to a different project
// than the git_id the rest of the CLI computes.

// originRemoteURLRegex captures the origin remote's url value from a git config file.
var originRemoteURLRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`\[remote "origin"\][^\[]*url\s*=\s*([^\n\r]+)`)

// NormalizeGitRemoteURL reduces a git remote URL to host/owner/repo so that the
// HTTPS, SSH and scheme-less spellings of one repository compare equal. It is
// the normalization the CLI hashes into a project's git_id.
func NormalizeGitRemoteURL(gitURL string) string {
	normalized := strings.TrimSuffix(gitURL, ".git")

	// scp-like SSH form (git@host:owner/repo or user@host:owner/repo) becomes host/path.
	if strings.Contains(normalized, "@") && strings.Contains(normalized, ":") {
		parts := strings.SplitN(normalized, "@", 2)
		if len(parts) == 2 {
			hostAndPath := strings.SplitN(parts[1], ":", 2)
			if len(hostAndPath) == 2 {
				return hostAndPath[0] + "/" + hostAndPath[1]
			}
		}
	}

	// Any scheme (https://, git://, ssh://) is dropped so only host/path remains.
	if _, rest, ok := strings.Cut(normalized, "://"); ok {
		return rest
	}

	// Already host/owner/repo.
	return normalized
}

// GitOriginURL returns the origin remote URL of the repository containing dir,
// walking up to the git root first so a subdirectory of a repository resolves
// to that repository. Returns "" when dir is not inside a repository or the
// repository has no origin remote.
func GitOriginURL(dir string) string {
	root, ok := FindGitRoot(dir)
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	configPath := gitConfigPath(root)
	if configPath == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return readOriginURL(configPath)
}

// FindGitRoot walks up from dir to the nearest ancestor containing a .git entry and
// returns it. The .git entry may be a directory (normal clone) or a file (git
// worktree or submodule); both satisfy the search. Returns false if no .git is
// found before the filesystem root.
func FindGitRoot(dir string) (string, bool) {
	if abs, err := filepath.Abs(dir); err == nil {
		dir = abs
	}
	dir = filepath.Clean(dir)
	for {
		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, ".git")); err == nil {
			return dir, true
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
		if parent == dir {
			return "", false
		}
		dir = parent
	}
}

// readOriginURL returns the origin remote URL from a git config file, or "" if the
// file is unreadable or has no origin remote.
func readOriginURL(gitConfigPath string) string {
	gitConfig, err := os.ReadFile(gitConfigPath)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	matches := originRemoteURLRegex.FindSubmatch(gitConfig)
	if len(matches) < 2 {
		return ""
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(string(matches[1]))
}

// gitConfigPath returns the path to the git config file that holds a root's
// remotes, handling both a normal .git directory and a .git file (worktrees and
// submodules, whose private gitdir points at a commondir that holds the shared
// config). Returns "" when it cannot be resolved.
func gitConfigPath(gitRoot string) string {
	gitPath := filepath.Join(gitRoot, ".git")
	info, err := os.Stat(gitPath)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	if info.IsDir() {
		return filepath.Join(gitPath, "config")
	}

	// A .git file reads "gitdir: <path>" and points at the worktree's private git
	// dir; the shared config lives in the common dir, not that private dir.
	data, err := os.ReadFile(gitPath)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	content := strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
	if !strings.HasPrefix(content, "gitdir:") {
		return ""
	}
	gitDir := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(content, "gitdir:"))
	if gitDir == "" {
		return ""
	}
	if !filepath.IsAbs(gitDir) {
		gitDir = filepath.Join(gitRoot, gitDir)
	}
	commonDir := gitDir
	if cd, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(gitDir, "commondir")); err == nil {
		c := strings.TrimSpace(string(cd))
		if !filepath.IsAbs(c) {
			c = filepath.Join(gitDir, c)
		}
		commonDir = filepath.Clean(c)
	}
	return filepath.Join(commonDir, "config")
}
```

```go
// writeGitConfig creates dir/.git/config naming origin, returning dir.
func writeGitConfig(t *testing.T, dir, origin string) string {
	t.Helper()
	gitDir := filepath.Join(dir, ".git")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(gitDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	config := "[core]\n\tbare = false\n"
	if origin != "" {
		config += "[remote \"origin\"]\n\turl = " + origin + "\n\tfetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*\n"
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(gitDir, "config"), []byte(config), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return dir
}

func TestGitOriginURL(t *testing.T) {
	const origin = "git@github.com:specstoryai/cloud-agent-test.git"

	t.Run("repository root", func(t *testing.T) {
		root := writeGitConfig(t, t.TempDir(), origin)
		if got := GitOriginURL(root); got != origin {
			t.Errorf("GitOriginURL = %q, want %q", got, origin)
		}
	})

	t.Run("subdirectory walks up to the root", func(t *testing.T) {
		root := writeGitConfig(t, t.TempDir(), origin)
		sub := filepath.Join(root, "a", "b")
		if err := os.MkdirAll(sub, 0o755); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if got := GitOriginURL(sub); got != origin {
			t.Errorf("GitOriginURL = %q, want %q", got, origin)
		}
	})

	t.Run("worktree .git file follows commondir", func(t *testing.T) {
		main := writeGitConfig(t, filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "main"), origin)
		private := filepath.Join(main, ".git", "worktrees", "wt")
		if err := os.MkdirAll(private, 0o755); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(private, "commondir"), []byte("../..\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		worktree := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "wt")
		if err := os.MkdirAll(worktree, 0o755); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(worktree, ".git"), []byte("gitdir: "+private+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {

		}

			t.Errorf("GitOriginURL = %q, want %q", got, origin)
		}
	})

	t.Run("no origin remote", func(t *testing.T) {
		root := writeGitConfig(t, t.TempDir(), "")
		if got := GitOriginURL(root); got != "" {
			t.Errorf("GitOriginURL = %q, want empty", got)
		}
	})
}
```

```text
package spi

import (
	"bufio"
	"errors"
)

// MaxRecordLineSize bounds how much memory a single JSONL record may consume.
// A line past it is treated as a corrupt or hostile file and discarded, so the
// bound has to sit above the largest record an agent legitimately writes: a
// tool result carrying a whole file, or a turn with a base64 image inlined into
// the record, both of which run to tens of megabytes. 64MB clears those with
// room to spare while still capping one record far below the machine.
const MaxRecordLineSize = 64 * 1024 * 1024

// ReadRecordLine reads one newline-terminated JSONL record from reader,
// returning the record (including its trailing newline), whether it exceeded
// limit, and the read error, which is io.EOF on the final record.
//
// The size test runs before each fragment is appended rather than against the
// finished line, because a cap applied after bufio.Reader.ReadString has
// returned has already allocated the whole oversized record. That is the
// allocation the cap exists to prevent.
//
// An oversized record is drained through its newline and reported through the
// second return value, so the records on either side of it still parse. Callers
// log it at Warn with the file and line and carry on: one unreadable record
// must not cost the user the rest of a session.
func ReadRecordLine(reader *bufio.Reader, limit int) ([]byte, bool, error) {
	var line []byte
	oversized := false
	for {
		fragment, err := reader.ReadSlice('\n')
		if !oversized {
			if len(line)+len(fragment) > limit {
				// Drop what was accumulated; the record is discarded either way.
				oversized = true
				line = nil
			} else {
				// ReadSlice returns a view into the reader's buffer, so the
				// fragment must be copied before the next read overwrites it.
				line = append(line, fragment...)
			}
		}
		if !errors.Is(err, bufio.ErrBufferFull) {
			return line, oversized, err
		}
	}
}
```

```text
// maxDiffRunes caps a rendered edit diff; find/replace payloads can be whole

const maxDiffRunes = 2000

// formatToolAsMarkdown generates formatted markdown for a ToolInfo (input + output).
// Returns the inner content only (no <tool-use> tags - those are added by pkg/session).
// Also sets tool.Summary if a custom summary is needed.
func formatToolAsMarkdown(tool *ToolInfo) string {
	if tool == nil {
		return ""
	}

	// Build custom summary for certain tools (appending key parameters)
	var customSummary string
	switch tool.Name {
	case "read_file", "write_file", "edit_file":
		if path := inputAsString(tool.Input, "path"); path != "" {
			customSummary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, path)
		}
	case "read_memory", "add_memory", "edit_memory":
		if location := memoryLocation(tool.Input); location != "" {
			customSummary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, location)
		}
	case "search":
		if pattern := inputAsString(tool.Input, "pattern"); pattern != "" {
			customSummary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, pattern)
		}
	case "web_search":
		if query := inputAsString(tool.Input, "query"); query != "" {
			customSummary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, query)
		}
	}

	// Set custom summary on tool if we built one
	if customSummary != "" {
		tool.Summary = &customSummary
	}

	// Build body content only (no wrapper tags)
	body := strings.TrimSpace(formatToolBodyFromInput(tool))
	result := strings.TrimSpace(formatToolResultFromOutput(tool))

	var builder strings.Builder
	if body != "" {
		builder.WriteString("\n")
		builder.WriteString(body)
	}
	if result != "" {
		// A single leading newline when there is no body: the wrapper already
		// ends the <summary> line, so doubling here would stack blank lines.
		if body != "" {
			builder.WriteString("\n\n")
		} else {
			builder.WriteString("\n")
		}
		builder.WriteString(result)
	}
	if builder.Len() > 0 {
		builder.WriteString("\n")
	}

	return builder.String()
}

// extractPathHints extracts file paths from Muse tool call args. Every
// file-touching native tool names its target `path`; shell commands get the
// shared extractor, resolved against the call's own workdir.
func extractPathHints(input map[string]any, workspaceRoot string) []string {
	var paths []string

	if value := inputAsString(input, "path"); value != "" {
		paths = append(paths, spi.NormalizePath(value, workspaceRoot))
	}

	if command := inputAsString(input, "command"); command != "" {
		cwd := inputAsString(input, "workdir")
		if cwd == "" {
			cwd = workspaceRoot
		}
		for _, shellPath := range spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, cwd, workspaceRoot) {
			if !slices.Contains(paths, shellPath) {
				paths = append(paths, shellPath)
			}
		}
	}

	return paths
}
```

```go
package cursorcloud

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strconv"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Network constants. The request interval keeps every caller inside the
// documented 20-requests-per-minute limit of the Cloud Agents API; the API
// returns no rate-limit headers to pace against, so the client paces itself.
const (
	defaultAPIBaseURL = "https://api.cursor.com"
	requestInterval   = 3 * time.Second
	jsonTimeout       = 30 * time.Second
	maxRetries        = 4
	maxBackoff        = 60 * time.Second
	initialBackoff    = 5 * time.Second
	// listPageSize is the API's maximum page size for GET /v1/agents.
	listPageSize = 100
)

// apiBaseURL is a variable so tests can point the client at an httptest server.
var apiBaseURL = defaultAPIBaseURL

// streamIdleTimeout bounds how long a stream read may see no bytes before the
// connection is treated as dead. The live stream sends a heartbeat event while
// the agent is quiet, so 90 seconds of silence means the connection is gone.
// A variable so tests can shorten it.
var streamIdleTimeout = 90 * time.Second

// errStreamExpired reports a 410 from the run stream endpoint: the stream is
// retained for 24 hours after a run ends and is gone afterwards.
var errStreamExpired = errors.New("run stream expired")

// apiError is a non-success HTTP response from the Cloud Agents API, carrying
// the error envelope the API returns ({"error":{"code","message"}}).
type apiError struct {
	Status  int
	Code    string
	Message string
}

func (e *apiError) Error() string {
	if e.Message != "" {
		return fmt.Sprintf("cursor api: HTTP %d %s: %s", e.Status, e.Code, e.Message)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("cursor api: HTTP %d", e.Status)
}

// isNotFound reports whether err is a 404 from the API.
func isNotFound(err error) bool {
	var ae *apiError
	return errors.As(err, &ae) && ae.Status == http.StatusNotFound
}

// rateLimiter spaces requests at least interval apart across every caller in
// the process: sync, watch polling and live streams all draw from one budget
// because the API limit is per key, not per connection.
type rateLimiter struct {
	mu       sync.Mutex
	interval time.Duration
	next     time.Time
	now      func() time.Time
	sleep    func(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error
}

func newRateLimiter(interval time.Duration) *rateLimiter {
	return &rateLimiter{interval: interval, now: time.Now, sleep: sleepContext}
}

// wait blocks until the caller may send its request, reserving the slot before
// sleeping so concurrent callers queue behind each other instead of all waking
// at the same instant.
func (l *rateLimiter) wait(ctx context.Context) error {
	l.mu.Lock()
	now := l.now()
	slot := l.next
	if slot.Before(now) {
		slot = now
	}
	l.next = slot.Add(l.interval)
	l.mu.Unlock()

	if d := slot.Sub(now); d > 0 {
		return l.sleep(ctx, d)
	}
	return nil
}

// holdUntil pushes every future slot to at least t, so a 429 seen by one
// caller also slows the others rather than letting them hit the limit again.
func (l *rateLimiter) holdUntil(t time.Time) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	if l.next.Before(t) {
		l.next = t
	}
	l.mu.Unlock()
}

// sleepContext sleeps for d or until ctx is done.
func sleepContext(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error {
	timer := time.NewTimer(d)
	defer timer.Stop()
	select {
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return ctx.Err()
	case <-timer.C:
		return nil
	}
}

// sharedLimiter is the process-wide request budget.
var sharedLimiter = newRateLimiter(requestInterval)

// apiClient talks to the Cloud Agents API with one key.
type apiClient struct {
	key        string
	baseURL    string
	jsonHTTP   *http.Client
	streamHTTP *http.Client
	limiter    *rateLimiter
}

// newAPIClient builds a client for key. JSON calls carry a whole-request
// timeout; stream calls cannot (a live run streams for minutes), so they rely
// on the idle deadline in openStream instead.
func newAPIClient(key string) *apiClient {
	return &apiClient{
		key:        key,
		baseURL:    apiBaseURL,
		jsonHTTP:   &http.Client{Timeout: jsonTimeout},
		streamHTTP: &http.Client{},
		limiter:    sharedLimiter,
	}
}

// do sends one request built by build, waiting for the rate limiter first and
// retrying 429 and 5xx responses with Retry-After or exponential backoff. A
// 2xx response is returned open; anything else is returned as *apiError.
func (c *apiClient) do(ctx context.Context, httpClient *http.Client, build func(ctx context.Context) (*http.Request, error)) (*http.Response, error) {
	backoff := initialBackoff
	for attempt := 0; ; attempt++ {
		if err := c.limiter.wait(ctx); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		req, err := build(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+c.key)
		resp, err := httpClient.Do(req)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if resp.StatusCode >= 200 && resp.StatusCode < 300 {
			return resp, nil
		}

		apiErr := readAPIError(resp)
		retryable := resp.StatusCode == http.StatusTooManyRequests || resp.StatusCode >= 500
		if !retryable || attempt >= maxRetries {
			return nil, apiErr
		}

		delay := retryAfter(resp.Header.Get("Retry-After"), c.limiter.now())
		if delay <= 0 {
			delay = backoff
			backoff = min(backoff*2, maxBackoff)
		}
		slog.Warn("Cursor API request throttled or failed, retrying",
			"path", req.URL.Path, "status", resp.StatusCode, "delay", delay, "attempt", attempt+1)
		c.limiter.holdUntil(c.limiter.now().Add(delay))
	}
}

// readAPIError drains and closes resp, decoding the API's error envelope.
func readAPIError(resp *http.Response) *apiError {
	defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
	apiErr := &apiError{Status: resp.StatusCode}
	// The error envelope is small; the cap only guards against a proxy page.
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 64*1024))
	var envelope struct {
		Error struct {
			Code    string `json:"code"`
			Message string `json:"message"`
		} `json:"error"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(body, &envelope) == nil {
		apiErr.Code = envelope.Error.Code
		apiErr.Message = envelope.Error.Message
	}
	return apiErr
}

// retryAfter parses a Retry-After header, either delay-seconds or an HTTP
// date, returning zero when the header is absent or unparseable.
func retryAfter(header string, now time.Time) time.Duration {
	if header == "" {
		return 0
	}
	if secs, err := strconv.Atoi(header); err == nil && secs > 0 {
		return time.Duration(secs) * time.Second
	}
	if t, err := http.ParseTime(header); err == nil {
		return t.Sub(now)
	}
	return 0
}

// getJSON fetches path and returns the raw response body. Raw bytes are kept
// rather than a typed decode so the mirror preserves fields this provider does
// not know about.
func (c *apiClient) getJSON(ctx context.Context, path string) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	resp, err := c.do(ctx, c.jsonHTTP, func(ctx context.Context) (*http.Request, error) {
		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, c.baseURL+path, nil)
		if err == nil {
			req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
		}
		return req, err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
	body, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if !json.Valid(body) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read %s: response is not JSON", path)
	}
	return json.RawMessage(body), nil
}

// me probes the key's identity; Check uses it as the installation test.
func (c *apiClient) me(ctx context.Context) (apiMe, error) {
	raw, err := c.getJSON(ctx, "/v1/me")
	if err != nil {
		return apiMe{}, err
	}
	var me apiMe
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &me); err != nil {
		return apiMe{}, fmt.Errorf("decode /v1/me: %w", err)
	}
	return me, nil
}

// listAgents returns every agent the key can see, newest first, following
// nextCursor. maxPages bounds the walk; zero means no bound.
func (c *apiClient) listAgents(ctx context.Context, maxPages int) ([]agentRecord, error) {
	var records []agentRecord
	cursor := ""
	for page := 0; maxPages == 0 || page < maxPages; page++ {
		query := url.Values{"limit": {strconv.Itoa(listPageSize)}}
		if cursor != "" {
			query.Set("cursor", cursor)
		}
		raw, err := c.getJSON(ctx, "/v1/agents?"+query.Encode())
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		var list struct {
			Items      []json.RawMessage `json:"items"`
			NextCursor string            `json:"nextCursor"`
		}
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &list); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode agent list: %w", err)
		}
		for _, item := range list.Items {
			record, err := decodeAgent(item)
			if err != nil {
				slog.Warn("Skipping undecodable agent in list", "error", err)
				continue
			}
			records = append(records, record)
		}
		if list.NextCursor == "" {
			break
		}
		cursor = list.NextCursor
	}
	return records, nil
}

// getAgent fetches one agent.
func (c *apiClient) getAgent(ctx context.Context, agentID string) (agentRecord, error) {
	raw, err := c.getJSON(ctx, "/v1/agents/"+url.PathEscape(agentID))
	if err != nil {
		return agentRecord{}, err
	}
	return decodeAgent(raw)
}

// listRuns returns every run of an agent, following nextCursor when present.
func (c *apiClient) listRuns(ctx context.Context, agentID string) ([]runRecord, error) {
	var records []runRecord
	cursor := ""
	for {
		path := "/v1/agents/" + url.PathEscape(agentID) + "/runs"
		if cursor != "" {
			path += "?" + url.Values{"cursor": {cursor}}.Encode()
		}
		raw, err := c.getJSON(ctx, path)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		var list struct {
			Items      []json.RawMessage `json:"items"`
			NextCursor string            `json:"nextCursor"`
		}
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &list); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode run list: %w", err)
		}
		for _, item := range list.Items {
			record, err := decodeRun(item)
			if err != nil {
				slog.Warn("Skipping undecodable run in list", "agentId", agentID, "error", err)
				continue
			}
			records = append(records, record)
		}
		if list.NextCursor == "" {
			return records, nil
		}
		cursor = list.NextCursor
	}
}

// conversation fetches the text-only v0 transcript, which outlives the stream.
func (c *apiClient) conversation(ctx context.Context, agentID string) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	return c.getJSON(ctx, "/v0/agents/"+url.PathEscape(agentID)+"/conversation")
}

// usage fetches token and cost usage for an agent.
func (c *apiClient) usage(ctx context.Context, agentID string) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	return c.getJSON(ctx, "/v1/agents/"+url.PathEscape(agentID)+"/usage")
}

// openStream opens a run's SSE stream. lastEventID, when set, resumes after
// that event. The returned body cancels its request once no bytes arrive for
// streamIdleTimeout, so a silently dropped connection surfaces as a read error
// instead of hanging forever. A 410 maps to errStreamExpired.
func (c *apiClient) openStream(ctx context.Context, agentID, runID, lastEventID string) (io.ReadCloser, error) {
	streamCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	path := "/v1/agents/" + url.PathEscape(agentID) + "/runs/" + url.PathEscape(runID) + "/stream"
	resp, err := c.do(streamCtx, c.streamHTTP, func(ctx context.Context) (*http.Request, error) {
		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, c.baseURL+path, nil)
		if err == nil {
			req.Header.Set("Accept", "text/event-stream")
			if lastEventID != "" {
				req.Header.Set("Last-Event-ID", lastEventID)
			}
		}
		return req, err
	})
	if err != nil {
		cancel()
		var ae *apiError
		if errors.As(err, &ae) && ae.Status == http.StatusGone {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", errStreamExpired, ae.Message)
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	return newIdleReader(resp.Body, cancel, streamIdleTimeout), nil
}

// idleReader cancels its request when no read has returned data for the idle
// period. Cancelling the request context makes the blocked Read return.
type idleReader struct {
	body   io.ReadCloser
	cancel context.CancelFunc
	timer  *time.Timer
	idle   time.Duration
}

func newIdleReader(body io.ReadCloser, cancel context.CancelFunc, idle time.Duration) *idleReader {
	return &idleReader{body: body, cancel: cancel, timer: time.AfterFunc(idle, cancel), idle: idle}
}

func (r *idleReader) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
	n, err := r.body.Read(p)
	if n > 0 {
		r.timer.Reset(r.idle)
	}
	return n, err
}

func (r *idleReader) Close() error {
	r.timer.Stop()
	r.cancel()
	return r.body.Close()
}
```

```go
}

type apiRepo struct {
	URL string `json:"url"`
}

// apiRun is the subset of a v1 run object the provider reads.
type apiRun struct {
	ID         string `json:"id"`
	AgentID    string `json:"agentId"`
	Status     string `json:"status"`
	CreatedAt  string `json:"createdAt"`
	UpdatedAt  string `json:"updatedAt"`
	DurationMs int64  `json:"durationMs"`
	Git        struct {
		Branches []struct {
			RepoURL string `json:"repoUrl"`
			Branch  string `json:"branch"`
			PrURL   string `json:"prUrl"`
		} `json:"branches"`
	} `json:"git"`
}

// isTerminal reports whether a run status is final. The non-terminal statuses
// observed are CREATING and RUNNING; anything else is treated as terminal so an
// unfamiliar final status never keeps a live stream attached forever.
func (r apiRun) isTerminal() bool {
	return r.Status != "CREATING" && r.Status != "RUNNING"
}

// v0Conversation is GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation: text-only messages for
// every run of the agent, in order.
type v0Conversation struct {
	ID       string      `json:"id"`
	Messages []v0Message `json:"messages"`
}

type v0Message struct {
	ID   string `json:"id"`
	Type string `json:"type"`
	Text string `json:"text"`
}

// agentRecord pairs a decoded agent with its native bytes.
type agentRecord struct {
	raw   json.RawMessage
	agent apiAgent
}

// runRecord pairs a decoded run with its native bytes.
type runRecord struct {
	raw json.RawMessage
	run apiRun
}

func decodeAgent(raw json.RawMessage) (agentRecord, error) {
	var agent apiAgent
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &agent); err != nil {
		return agentRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("decode agent: %w", err)
	}
	if !validAgentID(agent.ID) {
		return agentRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("decode agent: unexpected id %q", agent.ID)
	}
	return agentRecord{raw: raw, agent: agent}, nil
}

func decodeRun(raw json.RawMessage) (runRecord, error) {
	var run apiRun
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &run); err != nil {
		return runRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("decode run: %w", err)
	}
	if !validRunID(run.ID) {
		return runRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("decode run: unexpected id %q", run.ID)
	}
	return runRecord{raw: raw, run: run}, nil
}

// sseEvent is one SSE block as the mirror stores it: one JSON object per line
// of a run's events file.
type sseEvent struct {
	ID    string          `json:"id,omitempty"`
	Event string          `json:"event"`
	Data  json.RawMessage `json:"data"`
}

// maxSSELineSize caps one SSE line, and so one block. A variable so tests can
// exercise the oversized path without allocating 64MB.
var maxSSELineSize = spi.MaxRecordLineSize

// readSSE parses an SSE byte stream, calling emit for each complete block in
// order. A block holding an oversized line is skipped with a warning rather
// than ending the stream. Comment lines (": keepalive") are ignored. emit
// returning false stops the read early (used once the done event arrives).
func readSSE(r io.Reader, source string, emit func(sseEvent) bool) error {
	reader := bufio.NewReader(r)
	var id, event string
	var data strings.Builder
	hasData, skipBlock := false, false
	lineNo := 0

	dispatch := func() bool {
		defer func() {
			id, event = "", ""
			data.Reset()
			hasData, skipBlock = false, false
		}()
		if skipBlock {
			slog.Warn("Skipping oversized SSE block", "source", source, "line", lineNo)
			return true
		}
		if event == "" && !hasData {
			return true
		}
		if event == "" {
			// The SSE default event type; never observed from this API.
			event = "message"
		}
		return emit(sseEvent{ID: id, Event: event, Data: sseData(data.String(), hasData)})
	}

	for {
		line, oversized, err := spi.ReadRecordLine(reader, maxSSELineSize)
		if len(line) > 0 || oversized {
			lineNo++
		}
		if oversized {
			skipBlock = true
		} else if len(line) > 0 || err == nil {
			text := strings.TrimRight(string(line), "\r\n")
			if text == "" {
				if !dispatch() {
					return nil
				}
			} else if !strings.HasPrefix(text, ":") {
				field, value, _ := strings.Cut(text, ":")
				value = strings.TrimPrefix(value, " ")
				switch field {
				case "id":
					id = value
				case "event":
					event = value
				case "data":
					if hasData {
						data.WriteString("\n")
					}
					data.WriteString(value)
					hasData = true
				}
			}
		}
		if err != nil {
			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
				dispatch()
				return nil
			}
			return err
		}
	}
}

// sseData keeps a data payload as JSON. Every payload observed is a JSON
// object; anything else is preserved as a JSON string so no content is lost.
func sseData(text string, hasData bool) json.RawMessage {
	if !hasData {
		return nil
	}
	if json.Valid([]byte(text)) {
		return json.RawMessage(text)
	}
	quoted, _ := json.Marshal(text)
	return quoted
}

// eventsAreWhole reports whether a run's recorded events end with the done
// event, which the stream sends only after the run's final result.
func eventsAreWhole(events []sseEvent) bool {
	return len(events) > 0 && events[len(events)-1].Event == "done"
}

// encodeEvents renders events as JSONL for the mirror.
func encodeEvents(events []sseEvent) ([]byte, error) {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	for _, event := range events {
		line, err := json.Marshal(event)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		buf.Write(line)
		buf.WriteByte('\n')
	}
	return buf.Bytes(), nil
}

// readEventsFile reads a run's mirrored events. A missing file is no events.
// Malformed or oversized lines are skipped with a warning so one bad record
// costs one event, not the run.
func readEventsFile(path string) ([]sseEvent, error) {
	f, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return nil, nil
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()

	var events []sseEvent
	reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
	for lineNo := 1; ; lineNo++ {
		line, oversized, err := spi.ReadRecordLine(reader, spi.MaxRecordLineSize)
		if oversized {
			slog.Warn("Skipping oversized JSONL line", "file", path, "line", lineNo)
		} else if trimmed := bytes.TrimSpace(line); len(trimmed) > 0 {
			var event sseEvent
			if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal(trimmed, &event); jsonErr != nil || event.Event == "" {
				slog.Warn("Skipping corrupted JSONL line", "file", path, "line", lineNo, "error", jsonErr)
			} else {
				events = append(events, event)
			}
		}
		if err != nil {
			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
				return events, nil
			}
			return events, err
		}
	}
}

// eventTime converts an SSE id ("<epochMillis>-<seq>") to an RFC 3339 UTC
// timestamp. The id is the only timestamp the stream carries. Returns "" when
// the id is absent (status events carry none) or malformed.
func eventTime(id string) string {
	t, ok := eventInstant(id)
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	return spi.RFC3339Millis(t)
}

// eventInstant parses the epoch-millisecond prefix of an SSE id.
func eventInstant(id string) (time.Time, bool) {
	millis, _, _ := strings.Cut(id, "-")
	ms, err := strconv.ParseInt(millis, 10, 64)
	if err != nil || ms <= 0 {
		return time.Time{}, false
	}
	return time.UnixMilli(ms).UTC(), true
}

// validAgentID and validRunID guard ids before they become mirror path
// components; ids come from the network and are untrusted. Observed shapes are
// bc-<uuid> and run-<uuid>.
func validAgentID(id string) bool { return validPrefixedID(id, "bc-") }
func validRunID(id string) bool   { return validPrefixedID(id, "run-") }

func validPrefixedID(id, prefix string) bool {
	rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(id, prefix)
	if !ok || rest == "" || len(rest) > 64 {
		return false
	}
	for _, r := range rest {
		isHex := (r >= '0' && r <= '9') || (r >= 'a' && r <= 'f') || (r >= 'A' && r <= 'F')
		if !isHex && r != '-' {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}
```

```go
package cursorcloud

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

// maxResultRunes caps a rendered tool result. Results (file contents, command
// output, fetched pages) can be arbitrarily large; the mirror and RawData keep
// the full value, so the markdown preview is capped with a visible marker.
const maxResultRunes = 50000

// plumbingInputKeys are identifiers the harness copies into tool arguments on
// every call (observed on run_terminal_cmd); they say nothing about the call.
var plumbingInputKeys = []string{"toolCallId", "conversationId", "requestId"}

// shellInputNoise are run_terminal_cmd arguments that restate the command
// (parsingResult, simpleCommands) or are harness execution settings identical
// on every observed call (timeouts, output thresholds, stdin handling).
var shellInputNoise = []string{
	"parsingResult", "simpleCommands", "timeout", "hardTimeout",
	"timeoutBehavior", "fileOutputThresholdBytes", "closeStdin",
}

// toolType classifies a tool by the name recorded in tool_call events. Every
// name here was observed in a captured stream; see examples/tools.txt.
func toolType(name string) string {
	switch name {
	case "run_terminal_cmd":
		return schema.ToolTypeShell
	case "read_file", "web_fetch":
		return schema.ToolTypeRead
	case "edit_file", "delete_file":
		return schema.ToolTypeWrite
	case "file_search", "grep_search", "web_search":
		return schema.ToolTypeSearch
	case "todo_write":
		return schema.ToolTypeTask
	// Agent-state and harness tools: MCP plumbing, background waits, canvases,
	// generated assets, pull request management (seen in the research spike).
	case "mcp", "get_mcp_tools", "await", "generate_image",
		"write_canvas", "read_canvas", "pr_management":
		return schema.ToolTypeGeneric
	default:
		return schema.ToolTypeUnknown
	}
}

// cleanToolInput returns a copy of the recorded args without plumbing keys.
// Shell noise stays in the stored Input (it is real data) and is only hidden
// from the rendered body.
func cleanToolInput(args map[string]any) map[string]any {
	if args == nil {
		return nil
	}
	cleaned := make(map[string]any, len(args))
	for key, value := range args {
		if !containsString(plumbingInputKeys, key) {
			cleaned[key] = value
		}
	}
	return cleaned
}

// formatTool renders a tool call. It sets tool.Summary and returns the body
// that becomes FormattedMarkdown: the rendered input, then the rendered result.
// The VM's /workspace prefix is shown relative so paths read like the repo.
func formatTool(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
	if tool == nil {
		return ""
	}
	if summary := toolSummary(tool); summary != "" {
		tool.Summary = &summary
	}

	body := strings.TrimSpace(formatToolInput(tool))
	result := strings.TrimSpace(formatToolResult(tool))

	var b strings.Builder
	if body != "" {
		b.WriteString("\n")
		b.WriteString(body)
	}
	if result != "" {
		if body != "" {
			b.WriteString("\n\n")
		} else {
			b.WriteString("\n")
		}
		b.WriteString(result)
	}
	if b.Len() > 0 {
		b.WriteString("\n")
	}
	return b.String()
}

// toolSummary names the call and its key argument.
func toolSummary(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
	in := tool.Input
	var key string
	switch tool.Name {
	case "read_file", "edit_file", "delete_file":
		key = displayPath(spi.StringValue(in, "path"))
	case "run_terminal_cmd":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "description")
	case "file_search":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "globPattern")
	case "grep_search":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "pattern")
	case "web_search":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "searchTerm")
	case "web_fetch":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "url")
	case "mcp":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "name")
	case "get_mcp_tools":
		key = strings.Trim(spi.StringValue(in, "server")+"/"+spi.StringValue(in, "toolName"), "/")
	case "write_canvas":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "title")
	case "generate_image":
		key = displayPath(spi.StringValue(in, "filePath"))
	}
	if key == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** %s", tool.Name, spi.InlineCode(key))
}

// formatToolInput renders the arguments as labeled lines. Unenumerated tools
// fall back to pretty-printed JSON so no input is ever dropped.
func formatToolInput(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
	in := tool.Input
	switch tool.Name {
	case "run_terminal_cmd":
		return formatShellInput(in)
	case "read_file", "delete_file", "web_fetch", "web_search", "file_search":
		return formatLabeledInput(in, tool.Name)
	case "edit_file":
		return formatEditInput(tool)
	case "grep_search":
		return formatLabeledInput(in, tool.Name)
	case "todo_write":
		return formatTodos(in["todos"])
	case "mcp":
		return formatMCPInput(in)
	case "get_mcp_tools":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"server", "Server"}, {"toolName", "Tool"}})
	case "await":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"blockUntilMs", "Wait (ms)"}})
	case "generate_image":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"description", "Description"}, {"aspectRatio", "Aspect ratio"}, {"filePath", "File"}})
	case "write_canvas":
		var b strings.Builder
		if title := spi.StringValue(in, "title"); title != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Title: %s\n\n", title)
		}
		if contents := spi.StringValue(in, "contents"); contents != "" {
			b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence("jsx", contents))
		}
		return b.String()
	case "read_canvas":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"canvasId", "Canvas"}})
	default:
		return spi.RenderGenericJSON(in)
	}
}

// formatLabeledInput covers the tools whose summary already names the key
// argument; only the secondary arguments are worth a line.
func formatLabeledInput(in map[string]any, name string) string {
	switch name {
	case "file_search":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"targetDirectory", "Directory"}})
	case "grep_search":
		var b strings.Builder
		b.WriteString(labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"path", "Path"}, {"glob", "Glob"}}))
		var flags []string
		if v, _ := in["caseInsensitive"].(bool); v {
			flags = append(flags, "case-insensitive")
		}
		if v, _ := in["multiline"].(bool); v {
			flags = append(flags, "multiline")
		}
		if len(flags) > 0 {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Options: %s\n", strings.Join(flags, ", "))
		}
		return b.String()
	default:
		// read_file, delete_file, web_fetch, web_search: the summary carries it.
		return ""
	}
}

// labeledLines renders the given keys, in order, as "Label: value" lines.
// Path-valued labels are shown relative to the VM workspace.
func labeledLines(in map[string]any, keys [][2]string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, kv := range keys {
		value := spi.StringValue(in, kv[0])
		if value == "" {
			continue
		}
		if kv[0] == "path" || kv[0] == "targetDirectory" || kv[0] == "filePath" {
			value = displayPath(value)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s: %s\n", kv[1], spi.InlineCode(value))
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatShellInput shows the description, the command, and the directory
// when it is not the workspace root every observed call uses.
func formatShellInput(in map[string]any) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	command := spi.StringValue(in, "command")
	if dir := spi.StringValue(in, "workingDirectory"); dir != "" && dir != vmWorkspaceRoot {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Directory: %s\n\n", spi.InlineCode(displayPath(dir)))
	}
	if command != "" {
		b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence("bash", command))
	}
	// Anything beyond the known arguments is shown so a new argument is not lost.
	extra := spi.RenderGenericJSON(in, append([]string{"command", "workingDirectory", "description"}, shellInputNoise...)...)
	if extra != "" {
		b.WriteString("\n\n")
		b.WriteString(extra)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatEditInput prefers the diff the harness computed; while a call is still
// streaming (no result yet) the new content is the only record of the edit.
func formatEditInput(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
	if success := resultBranch(tool.Output, "success"); success != nil {
		if diff := spi.StringValue(success, "diffString"); diff != "" {
			return spi.CodeFence("diff", spi.CapRunes(diff, maxResultRunes))
		}
	}
	content := spi.StringValue(tool.Input, "streamContent")
	if content == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return spi.CodeFence(spi.LanguageFromPath(spi.StringValue(tool.Input, "path")), content)
}

// formatMCPInput names the server and tool; any further arguments render as JSON.
func formatMCPInput(in map[string]any) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"serverIdentifier", "Server"}, {"toolName", "Tool"}}))
	if extra := spi.RenderGenericJSON(in, "name", "serverIdentifier", "providerIdentifier", "toolName"); extra != "" {
		b.WriteString("\n")
		b.WriteString(extra)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// todoStatus maps the TODO_STATUS_* enum recorded by todo_write onto the
// shared checkbox vocabulary.
func todoStatus(status string) string {
	return strings.ToLower(strings.TrimPrefix(status, "TODO_STATUS_"))
}

// formatTodos renders a todo list; a malformed item is skipped.
func formatTodos(raw any) string {
	items, ok := raw.([]any)
	if !ok || len(items) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("Todo List:\n")
	for _, item := range items {
		todo, ok := item.(map[string]any)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		content := strings.TrimSpace(spi.StringValue(todo, "content"))
		if content == "" {
			continue
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- [%s] %s\n", spi.TodoSymbol(todoStatus(spi.StringValue(todo, "status"))), content)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatToolResult renders the result. Errors take priority for every tool;
// a shell command that exited non-zero records a "failure" branch instead.
func formatToolResult(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
	if tool.Output == nil {
		return ""
	}
	if errText := toolErrorText(tool.Output); errText != "" {
		return resultBlock("Error", errText)
	}

	if tool.Name == "run_terminal_cmd" {
		return formatShellResult(tool.Output)
	}

	success := resultBranch(tool.Output, "success")
	if success == nil {
		return formatGenericResult(tool.Output)
	}
	switch tool.Name {
	case "read_file":
		return formatReadResult(tool.Input, success)
	case "edit_file", "todo_write":
		// The body already shows the diff or the list.
		return ""
	case "delete_file":
		prev := spi.StringValue(success, "prevContent")
		if prev == "" {
			return "Result: deleted"
		}
		return "Result: deleted\n\n" + spi.FormatDiffBlock(spi.CapRunes(prev, maxResultRunes), "")
	case "file_search":
		return formatFileSearchResult(success)
	case "grep_search":
		return formatGrepResult(success)
	case "web_search":
		return formatWebSearchResult(success)
	case "web_fetch":
		if md := spi.StringValue(success, "markdown"); md != "" {
			return "Result:\n" + spi.CodeFence("markdown", spi.CapRunes(md, maxResultRunes))
		}
		return ""
	case "mcp":
		return formatMCPResult(success)
	case "get_mcp_tools":
		return formatMCPToolsResult(success)
	case "await":
		if complete, ok := success["complete"].(map[string]any); ok {
			if ms := spi.StringValue(complete, "runtimeMs"); ms != "" {
				return fmt.Sprintf("Result: completed after %s ms", ms)
			}
		}
		return formatGenericResult(tool.Output)
	case "generate_image":
		if path := spi.StringValue(success, "filePath"); path != "" {
			return "Result: saved to " + spi.InlineCode(path)
		}
		return ""
	case "write_canvas", "read_canvas":
		return formatCanvasResult(success)
	default:
		return formatGenericResult(tool.Output)
	}
}

// toolErrorText extracts a failed call's message. Observed shapes:
// {"error":{"error":"..."}} (delete_file, grep_search, web_fetch) and
// {"error":{"errorMessage":"..."}} (read_file). An error object with neither
// key is shown as JSON rather than dropped.
func toolErrorText(output map[string]any) string {
	errObj, ok := output["error"]
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	m, ok := errObj.(map[string]any)
	if !ok {
		if s, isString := errObj.(string); isString {
			return s
		}
		return compactJSON(errObj)
	}
	if text := spi.StringValue(m, "error", "errorMessage", "message"); text != "" {
		return text
	}
	return compactJSON(m)
}

// formatShellResult renders command output. A non-zero exit is recorded as a
// "failure" branch with exitCode and stderr; success carries stdout. The
// interleaved stream is preferred because it keeps stdout and stderr in the
// order the terminal showed them.
func formatShellResult(output map[string]any) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	branch := resultBranch(output, "success")
	if failure := resultBranch(output, "failure"); failure != nil {
		branch = failure
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Exit code: %s\n\n", spi.StringValue(failure, "exitCode"))
	}
	if branch == nil {
		return formatGenericResult(output)
	}
	if background, _ := output["isBackground"].(bool); background {
		b.WriteString("Running in the background.\n\n")
	}
	text := spi.StringValue(branch, "interleavedOutput")
	if text == "" {
		text = spi.StringValue(branch, "stdout") + spi.StringValue(branch, "stderr")
	}
	text = strings.Trim(spi.SanitizeShellOutput(text), "\n")
	if text == "" {
		b.WriteString("Result: (no output)")
		return b.String()
	}
	b.WriteString("Result:\n")
	b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence("text", spi.CapRunes(text, maxResultRunes)))
	return b.String()
}

// formatReadResult fences the file content by the file's language and notes
// when only part of the file was read.
func formatReadResult(in, success map[string]any) string {
	content := spi.StringValue(success, "content")
	if content == "" {
		return "Result: (empty file)"
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	if rng, ok := success["readRange"].(map[string]any); ok {
		start, end := spi.StringValue(rng, "startLine"), spi.StringValue(rng, "endLine")
		total := spi.StringValue(success, "totalLines")
		if start != "" && end != "" && !(start == "1" && end == total) {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Lines %s–%s of %s\n\n", start, end, total)
		}
	}
	path := spi.StringValue(in, "path")
	b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence(spi.LanguageFromPath(path), spi.CapRunes(strings.TrimRight(content, "\n"), maxResultRunes)))
	return b.String()
}

// formatFileSearchResult lists matched files.
func formatFileSearchResult(success map[string]any) string {
	files, _ := success["files"].([]any)
	if len(files) == 0 {
		return "Result: no files found"
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Result: %d %s\n", len(files), plural(len(files), "file", "files"))
	for _, f := range files {
		if name, ok := f.(string); ok {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s\n", spi.InlineCode(name))
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatGrepResult flattens workspaceResults into file:line: text lines. The
// map is keyed by workspace root; roots are sorted so output is deterministic.
func formatGrepResult(success map[string]any) string {
	roots, _ := success["workspaceResults"].(map[string]any)
	var lines []string
	for _, root := range sortedKeys(roots) {
		rootResult, _ := roots[root].(map[string]any)
		content, _ := rootResult["content"].(map[string]any)
		files, _ := content["matches"].([]any)
		for _, f := range files {
			file, ok := f.(map[string]any)
			if !ok {
				continue
			}
			name := spi.StringValue(file, "file")
			matches, _ := file["matches"].([]any)
			for _, m := range matches {
				match, ok := m.(map[string]any)
				if !ok {
					continue
				}
				lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s: %s", name, spi.StringValue(match, "lineNumber"), spi.StringValue(match, "content")))
			}
		}
	}
	if len(lines) == 0 {
		if roots == nil {
			return formatGenericResult(map[string]any{"success": success})
		}
		return "Result: no matches"
	}
	return "Result:\n" + spi.CodeFence("text", spi.CapRunes(strings.Join(lines, "\n"), maxResultRunes))
}

// formatWebSearchResult renders each reference. The chunk is already a
// markdown link list followed by a synthesis paragraph, so it is shown as is.
func formatWebSearchResult(success map[string]any) string {
	refs, _ := success["references"].([]any)
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, r := range refs {
		ref, ok := r.(map[string]any)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		chunk := strings.TrimSpace(spi.StringValue(ref, "chunk"))
		if chunk == "" {
			continue
		}
		if b.Len() > 0 {
			b.WriteString("\n\n")
		}
		b.WriteString(spi.CapRunes(chunk, maxResultRunes))
	}
	if b.Len() == 0 {
		return formatGenericResult(map[string]any{"success": success})
	}
	return "Result:\n\n" + b.String()
}

// formatMCPResult shows the text content parts. structuredContent repeats the
// text in every observed result, so it is shown only when there is no text.
func formatMCPResult(success map[string]any) string {
	parts, _ := success["content"].([]any)
	var texts []string
	for _, p := range parts {
		part, ok := p.(map[string]any)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		if textObj, ok := part["text"].(map[string]any); ok {
			if text := spi.StringValue(textObj, "text"); text != "" {
				texts = append(texts, text)
			}
		}
	}
	if len(texts) == 0 {
		return formatGenericResult(map[string]any{"success": success})
	}
	return "Result:\n" + spi.CodeFence("text", spi.CapRunes(strings.Join(texts, "\n\n"), maxResultRunes))
}

// formatMCPToolsResult shows a tool schema lookup. The content is a JSON
// string (a schema, or a note that output went to a file).
func formatMCPToolsResult(success map[string]any) string {
	content := spi.StringValue(success, "content")
	var b strings.Builder
	if path := spi.StringValue(success, "outputFilePath"); path != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Output file: %s\n\n", spi.InlineCode(path))
	}
	if content != "" {
		lang := "text"
		if json.Valid([]byte(content)) {
			lang = "json"
		}
		b.WriteString("Result:\n")
		b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence(lang, spi.CapRunes(content, maxResultRunes)))
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatCanvasResult links the canvas and shows its source when returned.
func formatCanvasResult(success map[string]any) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	title := spi.StringValue(success, "title")
	if url := spi.StringValue(success, "url"); url != "" {
		if title == "" {
			title = url
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Result: [%s](%s)\n", markdownLinkTextEscaper.Replace(title), url)
	}
	if source := spi.StringValue(success, "source"); source != "" {
		b.WriteString("\n")
		b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence("jsx", spi.CapRunes(source, maxResultRunes)))
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatGenericResult is the fallback for an unfamiliar result shape.
func formatGenericResult(output map[string]any) string {
	rendered := spi.RenderGenericJSON(output)
	if rendered == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return "Result:\n" + rendered
}

// resultBlock renders a labeled one-line or fenced multi-line result.
func resultBlock(label, text string) string {
	text = strings.TrimSpace(text)
	if strings.Contains(text, "\n") {
		return label + ":\n" + spi.CodeFence("text", spi.CapRunes(text, maxResultRunes))
	}
	return label + ": " + text
}

// resultBranch returns output[key] as an object, or nil.
func resultBranch(output map[string]any, key string) map[string]any {
	branch, _ := output[key].(map[string]any)
	return branch
}

// markdownLinkTextEscaper neutralizes the characters that would end a link's
// text early.
var markdownLinkTextEscaper = strings.NewReplacer("[", `\[`, "]", `\]`)

func compactJSON(v any) string {
	data, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	return string(data)
}

func sortedKeys(m map[string]any) []string {
	keys := make([]string, 0, len(m))
	for k := range m {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	sort.Strings(keys)
	return keys
}

func plural(n int, one, many string) string {
	if n == 1 {
		return one
	}
	return many
}

func containsString(list []string, s string) bool {
	for _, item := range list {
		if item == s {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
```
