package cursorcloud

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestReadSSE(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		input string
		want  []sseEvent
	}{
		{
			name:  "blocks with and without ids",
			input: "event: status\ndata: {\"status\":\"RUNNING\"}\n\nid: 1791904019438-1\nevent: thinking\ndata: {\"text\":\"a\"}\n\n",
			want: []sseEvent{
				{Event: "status", Data: []byte(`{"status":"RUNNING"}`)},
				{ID: "1791904019438-1", Event: "thinking", Data: []byte(`{"text":"a"}`)},
			},
		},
		{
			name:  "final block without a trailing blank line",
			input: "id: 1-0\nevent: done\ndata: {}",
			want:  []sseEvent{{ID: "1-0", Event: "done", Data: []byte(`{}`)}},
		},
		{
			name:  "comment lines and CRLF are ignored",
			input: ": keepalive\r\nevent: heartbeat\r\ndata: {}\r\n\r\n",
			want:  []sseEvent{{Event: "heartbeat", Data: []byte(`{}`)}},
		},
		{
			name:  "multi-line data joins with newlines and stays a string",
			input: "event: note\ndata: one\ndata: two\n\n",
			want:  []sseEvent{{Event: "note", Data: []byte(`"one\ntwo"`)}},
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got := parseSSEBytes(t, []byte(tt.input))
			if len(got) != len(tt.want) {
				t.Fatalf("got %d events %+v, want %d", len(got), got, len(tt.want))
			}
			for i := range got {
				if got[i].ID != tt.want[i].ID || got[i].Event != tt.want[i].Event || string(got[i].Data) != string(tt.want[i].Data) {
					t.Errorf("event %d = {%s %s %s}, want {%s %s %s}", i, got[i].ID, got[i].Event, got[i].Data, tt.want[i].ID, tt.want[i].Event, tt.want[i].Data)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestReadSSESkipsOversizedBlock(t *testing.T) {
	prev := maxSSELineSize
	maxSSELineSize = 64
	t.Cleanup(func() { maxSSELineSize = prev })

	input := "id: 1-0\nevent: assistant\ndata: {\"text\":\"" + strings.Repeat("x", 200) + "\"}\n\n" +
		"id: 2-0\nevent: assistant\ndata: {\"text\":\"kept\"}\n\n"
	got := parseSSEBytes(t, []byte(input))
	if len(got) != 1 || got[0].ID != "2-0" {
		t.Fatalf("got %+v, want only the block after the oversized one", got)
	}
}

func TestReadSSEStopsWhenEmitDeclines(t *testing.T) {
	input := "id: 1-0\nevent: done\ndata: {}\n\nid: 2-0\nevent: assistant\ndata: {}\n\n"
	var seen []string
	err := readSSE(strings.NewReader(input), "test", func(ev sseEvent) bool {
		seen = append(seen, ev.Event)
		return ev.Event != "done"
	})
	if err != nil || len(seen) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("seen %v err %v, want only done", seen, err)
	}
}

func TestReadEventsFileSkipsCorruptedLines(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "run.events.jsonl")
	content := `{"id":"1-0","event":"thinking","data":{"text":"a"}}` + "\n" +
		`{not json` + "\n" +
		`{"id":"2-0","data":{}}` + "\n" + // no event name: not a record this provider wrote
		`{"id":"3-0","event":"done","data":{}}` // final line without newline
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	events, err := readEventsFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(events) != 2 || events[0].ID != "1-0" || events[1].Event != "done" {
		t.Fatalf("events = %+v", events)
	}
	if !eventsAreWhole(events) {
		t.Error("a file ending in done should be whole")
	}
}

func TestEventsRoundTripThroughMirrorFile(t *testing.T) {
	fx := loadFixture(t, "fixture-run")
	events := parseSSEBytes(t, fx.streams[fx.runs[0].run.ID])
	m := mirror{root: t.TempDir()}
	if err := m.writeEvents("bc-1", "run-1", events); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	back, err := readEventsFile(m.eventsFile("bc-1", "run-1"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(back) != len(events) {
		t.Fatalf("round trip kept %d of %d events", len(back), len(events))
	}
	for i := range events {
		if back[i].ID != events[i].ID || back[i].Event != events[i].Event || string(back[i].Data) != string(events[i].Data) {
			t.Fatalf("event %d changed in the round trip", i)
		}
	}
}

package cursorcloud

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"flag"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

var updateGolden = flag.Bool("update", false, "rewrite golden session-data files")

// testWorkspace is the project root used for golden output. It is POSIX
// shaped on every OS because path hints are computed by shape.
const testWorkspace = "/project"

// snapshotFromFixture mirrors a fixture into a temp dir and reads it back,
// exercising the same read path the provider uses.
func snapshotFromFixture(t *testing.T, name string) *agentSnapshot {
	t.Helper()
	fx := loadFixture(t, name)
	m := mirror{root: t.TempDir()}
	writeFixtureMirror(t, m, fx)
	snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(m.agentDir(fx.agent.agent.ID))
	if err != nil || snap == nil {
		t.Fatalf("load snapshot: %v", err)
	}
	return snap
}

func marshalSession(t *testing.T, data *schema.SessionData) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	out, err := json.MarshalIndent(data, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return append(out, '\n')
}

func TestBuildSessionDataGolden(t *testing.T) {
	for _, name := range []string{"fixture-run", "tool-enumeration", "failure-run"} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			snap := snapshotFromFixture(t, name)
			data, _ := buildSessionData(snap, testWorkspace)
			if data == nil {
				t.Fatal("no session built")
			}
			if !data.Validate() {
				t.Error("session data failed schema validation")
			}
			got := marshalSession(t, data)

			// A second build of the same snapshot must change no bytes.
			again, _ := buildSessionData(snap, testWorkspace)
			if !bytes.Equal(got, marshalSession(t, again)) {
				t.Error("a second build produced different output")
			}

			golden := filepath.Join("testdata", name, "session-data.golden.json")
			if *updateGolden {
				if err := os.WriteFile(golden, got, 0o644); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
			}
			want, err := os.ReadFile(golden)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("read golden (run with -update to create): %v", err)
			}
			if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
				t.Errorf("session data differs from %s; run with -update after checking the change", golden)
			}
		})
	}
}

	if len(data.Exchanges) != 2 {

	}
	if data.Exchanges[0].ExchangeID != "run-ec41805a-07c4-4c80-874f-f077b9877582" {
		t.Errorf("first exchange is %s, want the earlier run first", data.Exchanges[0].ExchangeID)
	}
	if !strings.HasPrefix(firstPrompt, "Verification task for a transcript parser") {
		t.Errorf("first prompt = %q", firstPrompt)
	}
	if data.Slug != "verification-task-for-a" {
		t.Errorf("slug = %q", data.Slug)
	}
	if data.Provider.Version != "unknown" || data.Provider.ID != ProviderID {
		t.Errorf("provider = %+v", data.Provider)
	}

	if first.Messages[0].Role != schema.RoleUser || first.Messages[0].Timestamp != "2026-10-13T16:30:30.212Z" {

	}
	// The run opens with thinking then text, sharing one agent message.

		t.Errorf("second message parts = %+v, want thinking then text", parts)

	if first.Metadata["branch"] != "cursor/specstory-failure-capture-1e05" || first.Metadata["agentUrl"] == nil {

	}
	// The result event duplicates the final text; it must appear once.
	final := "Completed all six verification steps"
	count := 0
	for _, msg := range first.Messages {
		for _, part := range msg.Content {
			count += strings.Count(part.Text, final)
		}
	}
	if count != 1 {
		t.Errorf("final text rendered %d times, want once", count)
	}
}

func TestParseRunEventsToolMerging(t *testing.T) {
	ev := func(id, event, data string) sseEvent {
		return sseEvent{ID: id, Event: event, Data: json.RawMessage(data)}
	}
	tests := []struct {
		name       string
		events     []sseEvent
		wantArgs   string
		wantResult string
	}{
		{
			name: "running event without args, args arrive later",
			events: []sseEvent{
				ev("1-0", "tool_call", `{"callId":"c1","name":"edit_file","status":"running"}`),
				ev("2-0", "tool_call", `{"callId":"c1","name":"edit_file","status":"running","args":{"path":"/workspace/a.txt"}}`),
				ev("3-0", "tool_call", `{"callId":"c1","name":"edit_file","status":"completed","args":{"path":"/workspace/a.txt","streamContent":"x"},"result":{"success":{"linesAdded":1}}}`),
			},
			wantArgs:   `{"path":"/workspace/a.txt","streamContent":"x"}`,
			wantResult: `{"success":{"linesAdded":1}}`,
		},
		{
			// Observed on get_mcp_tools: a placeholder error rides a running
			// event while arguments stream, then the call completes.
			name: "provisional error on running event is replaced",
			events: []sseEvent{
				ev("1-0", "tool_call", `{"callId":"c1","name":"get_mcp_tools","status":"running","args":{"toolCallId":"unknown-tool-call-id"},"result":{"error":{"error":"Invalid arguments"}}}`),
				ev("2-0", "tool_call", `{"callId":"c1","name":"get_mcp_tools","status":"running","args":{"server":"cursor"}}`),
				ev("3-0", "tool_call", `{"callId":"c1","name":"get_mcp_tools","status":"completed","args":{"server":"cursor"},"result":{"success":{"content":"{}"}}}`),
			},
			wantArgs:   `{"server":"cursor"}`,
			wantResult: `{"success":{"content":"{}"}}`,
		},
		{
			name: "interrupted call keeps no provisional result",
			events: []sseEvent{
				ev("1-0", "tool_call", `{"callId":"c1","name":"get_mcp_tools","status":"running","args":{"server":"cursor"},"result":{"error":{"error":"Invalid arguments"}}}`),
			},
			wantArgs:   `{"server":"cursor"}`,
			wantResult: `null`,
		},
		{
			name: "completed error result is kept",
			events: []sseEvent{
				ev("1-0", "tool_call", `{"callId":"c1","name":"read_file","status":"running","args":{"path":"/workspace/x"}}`),
				ev("2-0", "tool_call", `{"callId":"c1","name":"read_file","status":"completed","args":{"path":"/workspace/x"},"result":{"error":{"errorMessage":"File not found"}}}`),
			},
			wantArgs:   `{"path":"/workspace/x"}`,
			wantResult: `{"error":{"errorMessage":"File not found"}}`,
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			transcript := parseRunEvents(tt.events, "test")
			if len(transcript.segments) != 1 || transcript.segments[0].call == nil {
				t.Fatalf("segments = %+v, want one tool call", transcript.segments)
			}
			call := transcript.segments[0].call
			if got := compactJSON(call.args); got != tt.wantArgs {
				t.Errorf("args = %s, want %s", got, tt.wantArgs)
			}
			if got := compactJSON(call.result); got != tt.wantResult {
				t.Errorf("result = %s, want %s", got, tt.wantResult)
			}
			if call.time != "1970-01-01T00:00:00.001Z" {
				t.Errorf("call time = %q, want the first event's time", call.time)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestParseRunEventsOrderingAndUnknowns(t *testing.T) {
	events := []sseEvent{
		{Event: "status", Data: json.RawMessage(`{"status":"RUNNING"}`)},
		{ID: "1000-0", Event: "interaction_update", Data: json.RawMessage(`{"type":"user-message-appended","userMessage":{"text":"hi"}}`)},
		{ID: "1001-0", Event: "thinking", Data: json.RawMessage(`{"text":"Let "}`)},
		{ID: "1001-0", Event: "interaction_update", Data: json.RawMessage(`{"type":"thinking-delta","text":"Let "}`)},
		{ID: "1002-0", Event: "thinking", Data: json.RawMessage(`{"text":"me"}`)},
		{ID: "1003-0", Event: "assistant", Data: json.RawMessage(`{"text":"Hello"}`)},
		{ID: "1004-0", Event: "brand_new_event", Data: json.RawMessage(`{}`)},
		{ID: "1005-0", Event: "interaction_update", Data: json.RawMessage(`{"type":"brand-new-type"}`)},
		{Event: "heartbeat", Data: json.RawMessage(`{}`)},
		{ID: "1006-0", Event: "assistant", Data: json.RawMessage(`{"text":" world"}`)},
		{ID: "1007-0", Event: "result", Data: json.RawMessage(`{"text":"Hello world"}`)},
		{ID: "1007-0", Event: "done", Data: json.RawMessage(`{}`)},
	}
	tr := parseRunEvents(events, "test")
	if tr.userText != "hi" || tr.startTime != "1970-01-01T00:00:01.000Z" || tr.resultTime != "1970-01-01T00:00:01.007Z" {
		t.Errorf("transcript = %+v", tr)
	}
	if len(tr.segments) != 2 || tr.segments[0].text.String() != "Let me" || tr.segments[1].text.String() != "Hello world" {
		var got []string
		for _, s := range tr.segments {
			got = append(got, s.text.String())
		}
		t.Errorf("segments = %q, want deltas concatenated per kind and unknown events ignored", got)
	}
}

func TestV0FallbackForExpiredPartialRun(t *testing.T) {
	snap := snapshotFromFixture(t, "failure-run")
	// Truncate the second run's capture as if the watcher stopped mid-run and
	// the stream expired before a sync could replay it.
	snap.runs[1].events = snap.runs[1].events[:40]
	// And drop the first run's capture entirely.
	snap.runs[0].events = nil

	data, _ := buildSessionData(snap, testWorkspace)
	for i, ex := range data.Exchanges {
		if ex.Metadata["source"] != "v0-conversation" {
			t.Errorf("exchange %d source = %v, want v0-conversation", i, ex.Metadata["source"])
		}
	}
	first := data.Exchanges[0]
	// Turn 0 starts with the agent's first user message, whose id is a bare UUID.
	if first.Messages[0].ID != "cde498a2-37da-4b54-b81f-82bc82341d4b" || first.Messages[0].Role != schema.RoleUser {
		t.Errorf("turn 0 first message = %+v", first.Messages[0])
	}
	if len(first.Messages) != 3 {
		t.Errorf("turn 0 has %d messages, want 3", len(first.Messages))
	}
	second := data.Exchanges[1]
	if second.Messages[0].ID != "turn-1:user" || len(second.Messages) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("turn 1 messages = %+v", second.Messages)
	}
	for _, msg := range append(first.Messages, second.Messages...) {
		if msg.Tool != nil {
			t.Error("the v0 fallback is text only")
		}
	}
}

	var decoded struct {
		Agent map[string]any `json:"agent"`
		Runs  []struct {
			Run    map[string]any `json:"run"`
			Events []sseEvent     `json:"events"`
		} `json:"runs"`
		Conversation map[string]any `json:"conversation"`
		Usage        map[string]any `json:"usage"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &decoded); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// env and workOnCurrentBranch are not read by the provider; they must survive.
	if decoded.Agent["env"] == nil || decoded.Agent["workOnCurrentBranch"] == nil {
		t.Error("unknown agent fields were dropped")
	}
	if len(decoded.Runs) != 2 || len(decoded.Runs[1].Events) != len(snap.runs[1].events) || decoded.Usage["cost"] == nil || decoded.Conversation["messages"] == nil {
		t.Error("raw data is missing runs, events, usage or conversation")
	}
}

package cursorcloud

import (
	"bufio"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

// expectedToolTypes is the classification of every name recorded in
// tool_call events (examples/tools.txt section 1).
var expectedToolTypes = map[string]string{
	"await":            schema.ToolTypeGeneric,
	"delete_file":      schema.ToolTypeWrite,
	"edit_file":        schema.ToolTypeWrite,
	"file_search":      schema.ToolTypeSearch,
	"generate_image":   schema.ToolTypeGeneric,
	"get_mcp_tools":    schema.ToolTypeGeneric,
	"grep_search":      schema.ToolTypeSearch,
	"mcp":              schema.ToolTypeGeneric,
	"read_canvas":      schema.ToolTypeGeneric,
	"read_file":        schema.ToolTypeRead,
	"run_terminal_cmd": schema.ToolTypeShell,
	"todo_write":       schema.ToolTypeTask,
	"web_fetch":        schema.ToolTypeRead,
	"web_search":       schema.ToolTypeSearch,
	"write_canvas":     schema.ToolTypeGeneric,
}

// recordedToolNames reads section 1 of examples/tools.txt.
func recordedToolNames(t *testing.T) []string {
	t.Helper()
	f, err := os.Open(filepath.Join("examples", "tools.txt"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
	var names []string
	inSection := false
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(f)
	for scanner.Scan() {
		line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "## 1."):
			inSection = true
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "## "):
			inSection = false
		case inSection && line != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(line, "#"):
			names = append(names, line)
		}
	}
	return names
}

func TestToolTypeSweep(t *testing.T) {
	names := recordedToolNames(t)
	if len(names) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no tool names read from examples/tools.txt")
	}
	for _, name := range names {
		want, ok := expectedToolTypes[name]
		if !ok {
			t.Errorf("%s is in tools.txt but has no expected type here", name)
			continue
		}
		if got := toolType(name); got != want {
			t.Errorf("toolType(%q) = %q, want %q", name, got, want)
		}
	}
	if got := toolType("never_seen_tool"); got != schema.ToolTypeUnknown {
		t.Errorf("an unenumerated tool is %q, want unknown", got)
	}
}

// renderedCalls converts every tool call in the captured fixtures through the
// production dispatch path.
func renderedCalls(t *testing.T) []schema.Message {
	t.Helper()
	var msgs []schema.Message
	for _, name := range []string{"fixture-run", "tool-enumeration", "failure-run"} {
		fx := loadFixture(t, name)
		runIDs := make([]string, 0, len(fx.streams))
		for id := range fx.streams {
			runIDs = append(runIDs, id)
		}
		sort.Strings(runIDs)
		for _, id := range runIDs {
			for _, seg := range parseRunEvents(parseSSEBytes(t, fx.streams[id]), name).segments {
				if seg.call != nil {
					msgs = append(msgs, toolMessage(seg.call, testWorkspace))
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return msgs
}

func TestCapturedToolCallsRender(t *testing.T) {
	// What every captured call of a tool must show, success or failure.
	expect := map[string][]string{
		"run_terminal_cmd": {"```bash", "Result"},
		"edit_file":        {"```diff"},
		"todo_write":       {"Todo List:\n- ["},
		"mcp":              {"Server: `cursor-", "Result:\n```text"},
		"get_mcp_tools":    {"Server: `cursor"},
		"await":            {"Result: completed after 1000 ms"},
		"generate_image":   {"Description: ", "Result: saved to `/opt/cursor/artifacts/assets/tool_demo_icon.jpg`"},
		"write_canvas":     {"```jsx", "Result: [Tool Demo Canvas](https://cursor.com/canvas/"},
		"read_canvas":      {"Canvas: ", "```jsx"},
		"file_search":      {"Directory: `.`", "Result: 1 file\n- `tools.txt`"},
		"web_search":       {"Result:\n\nLinks:\n1. [Cursor Agent](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview)"},
	}
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, msg := range renderedCalls(t) {
		tool := msg.Tool
		seen[tool.Name] = true
		if tool.Type == schema.ToolTypeUnknown {
			t.Errorf("%s classified unknown", tool.Name)
		}
		if tool.FormattedMarkdown == nil || strings.TrimSpace(*tool.FormattedMarkdown) == "" {
			t.Errorf("%s (%s) rendered nothing", tool.Name, tool.UseID)
			continue
		}
		md := *tool.FormattedMarkdown
		for _, want := range expect[tool.Name] {
			if !strings.Contains(md, want) {
				t.Errorf("%s (%s) markdown lacks %q:\n%s", tool.Name, tool.UseID, want, md)
			}
		}
		for _, key := range plumbingInputKeys {
			if _, ok := tool.Input[key]; ok {
				t.Errorf("%s input still carries %s", tool.Name, key)
			}
		}
		// Known tools never fall back to dumping their raw result envelope.
		if strings.Contains(md, `"success": {`) {
			t.Errorf("%s rendered its raw result envelope:\n%s", tool.Name, md)
		}
	}
	for _, name := range recordedToolNames(t) {
		if !seen[name] {
			t.Errorf("no captured call of %s was rendered", name)
		}
	}
}

func TestCapturedFailuresRenderTheError(t *testing.T) {
	// The failure-run capture's deliberate failures, keyed by call id.
	want := map[string]string{
		"read_file":   "Error: File not found",
		"delete_file": "Error: File not found: /workspace/missing-file.txt",
		"grep_search": "Error: Path does not exist: /nonexistent-path",
		"web_fetch":   "Error: Error fetching URL, status code: 500 Internal Server Error",
	}
	found := map[string]bool{}
	for _, msg := range renderedCalls(t) {
		md := ""
		if msg.Tool.FormattedMarkdown != nil {
			md = *msg.Tool.FormattedMarkdown
		}
		if text, ok := want[msg.Tool.Name]; ok && strings.Contains(md, text) {
			found[msg.Tool.Name] = true
		}
		if msg.Tool.Name == "run_terminal_cmd" && strings.Contains(md, "cat /nonexistent-file") {
			found["shell failure"] = true
			if !strings.Contains(md, "Exit code: 1") || !strings.Contains(md, "No such file or directory") {
				t.Errorf("shell failure lacks exit code or stderr:\n%s", md)
			}
		}
	}
	for name := range want {
		if !found[name] {
			t.Errorf("no %s call rendered %q", name, want[name])
		}
	}
	if !found["shell failure"] {
		t.Error("the failing shell command was not rendered")
	}
}

func TestFormatToolFallbacks(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		tool schema.ToolInfo
		want []string
	}{
		{
			name: "unknown tool renders input and result as JSON",
			tool: schema.ToolInfo{Name: "brand_new", Input: map[string]any{"a": "b"}, Output: map[string]any{"success": map[string]any{"x": 1.0}}},
			want: []string{"```json\n{\n  \"a\": \"b\"\n}", "Result:\n```json"},
		},
		{
			name: "error without a known message key",
			tool: schema.ToolInfo{Name: "read_file", Input: map[string]any{"path": "/workspace/a"}, Output: map[string]any{"error": map[string]any{"code": 7.0}}},
			want: []string{`Error: {"code":7}`},
		},
		{
			name: "unfamiliar result shape on a known tool",
			tool: schema.ToolInfo{Name: "read_file", Input: map[string]any{"path": "/workspace/a"}, Output: map[string]any{"pending": true}},
			want: []string{"Result:\n```json"},
		},
		{
			name: "edit still streaming shows its content",
			tool: schema.ToolInfo{Name: "edit_file", Input: map[string]any{"path": "/workspace/a.go", "streamContent": "package a"}},
			want: []string{"```go\npackage a\n```"},
		},
		{
			name: "malformed todo item is skipped",
			tool: schema.ToolInfo{Name: "todo_write", Input: map[string]any{"todos": []any{"bad", map[string]any{"content": "ok", "status": "TODO_STATUS_COMPLETED"}}}},
			want: []string{"Todo List:\n- [x] ok\n"},
		},
		{
			name: "background shell command",
			tool: schema.ToolInfo{Name: "run_terminal_cmd", Input: map[string]any{"command": "sleep 9"}, Output: map[string]any{"success": map[string]any{}, "isBackground": true}},
			want: []string{"Running in the background.", "Result: (no output)"},
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			tool := tt.tool
			md := formatTool(&tool)
			for _, want := range tt.want {
				if !strings.Contains(md, want) {
					t.Errorf("markdown lacks %q:\n%s", want, md)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

const testOrigin = "git@github.com:specstoryai/cloud-agent-test.git"

// makeProject creates a git checkout at dir whose origin is origin.
func makeProject(t *testing.T, dir, origin string) string {
	t.Helper()
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, ".git"), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	config := "[remote \"origin\"]\n\turl = " + origin + "\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, ".git", "config"), []byte(config), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return dir
}

	t.Run("no key is not found with guidance", func(t *testing.T) {
		useSettings(t, "")
		res := NewProvider().Check("")
		if res.Success || res.ErrorType != spi.CheckErrorNotFound || !strings.Contains(res.ErrorMessage, apiKeyPage) {
			t.Errorf("result = %+v", res)
		}
	})

		useSettings(t, "test-key")
		newFakeAPI(t)
		res := NewProvider().Check("")
		if !res.Success || res.Version != "unknown" || !strings.Contains(res.Location, `"Cloude Agent API key for SpecStory"`) || res.ErrorType != "" {
			t.Errorf("result = %+v", res)
		}

		useSettings(t, "")
		SetAPIKey("test-key")

		if res := NewProvider().Check(""); !res.Success {
			t.Errorf("result = %+v", res)

		f.meStatus = http.StatusUnauthorized
		res := NewProvider().Check("")

		t.Error("an unchanged agent was re-fetched")
	}
	if after := snapshotTree(t, mirrorRoot); after != before {
		t.Error("a sync with no activity changed the mirror")
	}

	// Once updatedAt advances the agent is re-fetched, but its whole streams are not.
	fx := loadFixture(t, "fixture-run")
	var agent map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(fx.agent.raw, &agent)
	agent["updatedAt"] = "2026-10-13T15:09:00.000Z"
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(agent)
	f.setAgent(raw)
	syncProject(t, project, false)
	if f.count("/v1/agents/bc-a2a25972-6529-47c0-9691-8f135d0a6527/runs") != runsBefore+1 {
		t.Error("an advanced updatedAt did not refresh the runs")
	}
	if f.count("/v1/agents/bc-a2a25972-6529-47c0-9691-8f135d0a6527/runs/") != streamsBefore {
		t.Error("a whole stream capture was fetched again")
	}
}

// snapshotTree fingerprints every file's bytes and mtime under root.
func snapshotTree(t *testing.T, root string) string {
	t.Helper()
	var b strings.Builder
	_ = filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
			return err
		}
		info, _ := d.Info()
		data, _ := os.ReadFile(path)
		b.WriteString(path + "|" + info.ModTime().String() + "|" + string(data) + "\n")
		return nil
	})
	return b.String()
}

func TestPartialCaptureReplacedWhileRetainedKeptAfterExpiry(t *testing.T) {
	fx := loadFixture(t, "fixture-run")
	runID := fx.runs[0].run.ID
	agentID := fx.agent.agent.ID
	full := parseSSEBytes(t, fx.streams[runID])

	for _, tt := range []struct {
		name      string
		expired   bool
		wantWhole bool
	}{
		{"retained stream replaces the partial capture", false, true},
		{"expired stream keeps the partial capture", true, false},
	} {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			useSettings(t, "test-key")
			f := newFakeAPI(t)
			f.addFixture(fx)
			f.expired[runID] = tt.expired
			m := mirror{root: t.TempDir()}
			writeFixtureMirror(t, m, fx)
			if err := m.writeEvents(agentID, runID, full[:50]); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			// The run ended an hour before "now", inside the 24h retention.
			ended, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, fx.runs[0].run.UpdatedAt)
			if err := m.refreshAgent(t.Context(), newAPIClient("test-key"), fx.agent, refreshOptions{now: ended.Add(time.Hour)}); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			events, _ := readEventsFile(m.eventsFile(agentID, runID))
			if eventsAreWhole(events) != tt.wantWhole {
				t.Errorf("whole = %v, want %v (%d events)", eventsAreWhole(events), tt.wantWhole, len(events))
			}
		})
	}

	t.Run("a stream past retention is not requested", func(t *testing.T) {
		useSettings(t, "test-key")
		f := newFakeAPI(t)
		f.addFixture(fx)
		m := mirror{root: t.TempDir()}
		writeFixtureMirror(t, m, fx)
		if err := m.writeEvents(agentID, runID, full[:50]); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		ended, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, fx.runs[0].run.UpdatedAt)
		if err := m.refreshAgent(t.Context(), newAPIClient("test-key"), fx.agent, refreshOptions{now: ended.Add(25 * time.Hour)}); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if n := f.count("/v1/agents/" + agentID + "/runs/" + runID + "/stream"); n != 0 {
			t.Errorf("requested an expired stream %d times", n)
		}
	})
}

func TestProjectPathShapes(t *testing.T) {
	useSettings(t, "")
	base := t.TempDir()
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		path func(real string) string
		skip func() string
	}{
		{"space and underscore in the path", func(real string) string { return real }, nil},
		{"reached through a symlink", func(real string) string {
			link := filepath.Join(base, "link")
			if err := os.Symlink(real, link); err != nil {
				return ""
			}
			return link
		}, nil},
		{"differently cased spelling", func(real string) string {
			return filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(real), strings.ToUpper(filepath.Base(real)))
		}, func() string {
			if runtime.GOOS == "linux" {
				return "case-sensitive filesystem"
			}
			return ""
		}},
	}
	real := makeProject(t, filepath.Join(base, "my project_dir"), testOrigin)
	m, _ := mirrorFor(real)
	writeFixtureMirror(t, m, loadFixture(t, "fixture-run"))

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if tt.skip != nil {
				if reason := tt.skip(); reason != "" {
					t.Skip(reason)
				}
			}
			path := tt.path(real)
			if path == "" {
				t.Skip("symlinks unavailable")
			}
			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err != nil {
				t.Skip("path does not resolve on this filesystem")
			}
			list, err := NewProvider().ListAgentChatSessions(path)
			if err != nil || len(list) != 1 {
				t.Errorf("found %d sessions (err %v), want the same one as the canonical path", len(list), err)
			}
		})
	}
}

package cursorcloud

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"

// fastWatcher shortens the watcher's timings so acceptance cases run quickly.
func fastWatcher(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	prevPoll, prevDebounce, prevReconnect := pollInterval, emitDebounce, reconnectDelay
	pollInterval, emitDebounce, reconnectDelay = 40*time.Millisecond, 20*time.Millisecond, 10*time.Millisecond
	t.Cleanup(func() { pollInterval, emitDebounce, reconnectDelay = prevPoll, prevDebounce, prevReconnect })
}

// emissions records delivered sessions.
type emissions struct {
	mu       sync.Mutex
	sessions []*spi.AgentChatSession
}

func (e *emissions) callback(s *spi.AgentChatSession) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.sessions = append(e.sessions, s)
}

func (e *emissions) all() []*spi.AgentChatSession {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]*spi.AgentChatSession(nil), e.sessions...)
}

// waitFor polls cond until it holds or the deadline passes.
func waitFor(t *testing.T, what string, cond func() bool) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for !cond() {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

// startWatcher starts a watcher for a fresh project and returns it with its
// emissions; stop is the caller's.
func startWatcher(t *testing.T) (*cloudWatcher, *emissions) {
	t.Helper()
	project := makeProject(t, t.TempDir(), testOrigin)
	got := &emissions{}
	w := newCloudWatcher(project, projectOrigin(project), newAPIClient("test-key"), false, got.callback)
	w.start(context.Background())
	return w, got
}

// withUpdatedAt returns a copy of an agent object with a new updatedAt.
func withUpdatedAt(t *testing.T, raw json.RawMessage, updatedAt string) json.RawMessage {
	t.Helper()
	var agent map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &agent); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	agent["updatedAt"] = updatedAt
	out, _ := json.Marshal(agent)
	return out
}

// liveStream rewrites a captured stream's ids to times after now, so its
// events count as activity, and splits it into blocks.
func liveStream(t *testing.T, data []byte) []string {
	t.Helper()
	idLine := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^id: (\d+)-(\d+)$`)
	first := int64(0)
	base := time.Now().Add(time.Second).UnixMilli()
	rewritten := idLine.ReplaceAllStringFunc(string(data), func(line string) string {
		m := idLine.FindStringSubmatch(line)
		ms, _ := strconv.ParseInt(m[1], 10, 64)
		if first == 0 {
			first = ms
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("id: %d-%s", base+ms-first, m[2])
	})
	var blocks []string
	for _, block := range strings.Split(rewritten, "\n\n") {
		if strings.TrimSpace(block) != "" {
			blocks = append(blocks, block+"\n\n")
		}
	}
	return blocks
}

func TestWatcherFollowsRunningRunLive(t *testing.T) {
	useSettings(t, "test-key")
	fastWatcher(t)
	f := newFakeAPI(t)
	fx := loadFixture(t, "fixture-run")
	runID := fx.runs[0].run.ID
	blocks := liveStream(t, fx.streams[runID])

	// The agent appears after startup with its run still RUNNING.
	running := func(status string) json.RawMessage {
		var run map[string]any
		_ = json.Unmarshal(fx.runs[0].raw, &run)
		run["status"] = status
		out, _ := json.Marshal(run)
		return out
	}

	pause := make(chan struct{})
	release := make(chan struct{})
	var requests []string
	f.streamHandler = func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, id string) {
		f.mu.Lock()
		requests = append(requests, r.Header.Get("Last-Event-ID"))
		attempt := len(requests)
		f.mu.Unlock()
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
		flusher := w.(http.Flusher)
		start := 0
		if attempt > 1 {
			// Resume after the Last-Event-ID, repeating its block as a server may.
			for i, b := range blocks {
				if strings.Contains(b, "id: "+r.Header.Get("Last-Event-ID")+"\n") {
					start = i
					break
				}
			}
		}
		for i := start; i < len(blocks); i++ {
			if attempt == 1 && i == len(blocks)/2 {
				// First connection: go quiet long enough for a debounced save,
				// then drop the connection mid-run.
				close(pause)
				<-release
				return
			}
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(blocks[i]))
			flusher.Flush()
		}
		f.mu.Lock()
		f.runs[fx.agent.agent.ID] = []json.RawMessage{running("FINISHED")}
		f.mu.Unlock()
	}

	w, got := startWatcher(t)
	waitFor(t, "the baseline", func() bool { return f.count("/v1/agents") >= 1 })
	f.mu.Lock()
	f.agents = append(f.agents, fx.agent.raw)
	f.runs[fx.agent.agent.ID] = []json.RawMessage{running("RUNNING")}
	f.convs[fx.agent.agent.ID] = fx.conversation
	f.usages[fx.agent.agent.ID] = fx.usage
	f.mu.Unlock()

	<-pause
	waitFor(t, "a save during the run", func() bool {
		for _, s := range got.all() {
			if len(s.SessionData.Exchanges) == 1 && len(s.SessionData.Exchanges[0].Messages) > 1 {
				return true
			}
		}
		return false
	})
	midRun := len(got.all()[len(got.all())-1].SessionData.Exchanges[0].Messages)
	close(release)

	waitFor(t, "the finished run", func() bool {
		all := got.all()
		last := all[len(all)-1]
		return last.SessionData.Exchanges[0].Metadata["status"] == "FINISHED"
	})
	w.stop()

	final := got.all()[len(got.all())-1]
	if n := len(final.SessionData.Exchanges[0].Messages); n <= midRun {
		t.Errorf("final save has %d messages, mid-run had %d", n, midRun)
	}
	m, _ := mirrorFor(w.projectPath)
	events, _ := readEventsFile(m.eventsFile(fx.agent.agent.ID, runID))
	if !eventsAreWhole(events) {
		t.Error("the mirrored capture is not whole after the run finished")
	}
	if len(events) != len(blocks) {
		t.Errorf("mirrored %d events, want %d: the resumed stream duplicated or lost events", len(events), len(blocks))
	}
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	if len(requests) < 2 || requests[0] != "" || requests[1] == "" {
		t.Errorf("stream requests Last-Event-ID = %q, want a fresh connect then a resume", requests)
	}
}

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Latest released version of the Cursor IDE.
#
# Channel: Cursor's official download API,
# https://cursor.com/api/download?platform=...&releaseTrack=stable — returns a
# JSON document with the current stable IDE version. The platform parameter is
# required but versions are released in lockstep across platforms;
# darwin-universal is used as the canonical probe.
#
# Requires jq (present on GitHub Actions runners).
#
# Factory SPI contract: print the current released version to stdout and exit 0.
# Non-zero exit means "sensor failure", never "no change". Output is opaque to
# the factory — byte-compared against the stored reading, never parsed.
set -euo pipefail
version=$(curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 --retry 2 --retry-delay 2 "https://cursor.com/api/download?platform=darwin-universal&releaseTrack=stable" \
  | jq -r '.version // empty')
if [ -z "$version" ]; then
  echo "could not read .version from cursor.com download API" >&2
  exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' "$version"
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Latest released version of Cursor CLI (cursor-agent).
#
# Channel: the official installer at https://cursor.com/install — Cursor CLI has
# no npm/brew/GitHub-releases channel; the installer script embeds the current
# version in its download URL (downloads.cursor.com/lab/<version>/...), so the
# installer itself is the release manifest.
#
# Factory SPI contract: print the current released version to stdout and exit 0.
# Non-zero exit means "sensor failure", never "no change". Output is opaque to
# the factory — byte-compared against the stored reading, never parsed.
set -euo pipefail
version=$(curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 --retry 2 --retry-delay 2 https://cursor.com/install \
  | sed -n 's|.*downloads\.cursor\.com/lab/\([^/]*\)/.*|\1|p' | head -1)
if [ -z "$version" ]; then
  echo "could not extract version from cursor.com/install (installer format changed?)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' "$version"
```

````markdown
# Cursor Cloud Agent session format

A Cursor Cloud Agent runs in Cursor's backend. Its conversation is never written to the user's machine, so the provider's native store is the Cloud Agents REST API at `https://api.cursor.com`, and a local mirror of that API is what every read path parses. Everything below was observed against the live API on 2026-10-13 (API `info.version` 1.0.0, v1 public beta plus legacy v0). The captures are in `testdata/` and `examples/captures/`.

## Baseline version

The API exposes no agent version. `CheckResult.Version` and `ProviderInfo.Version` are `"unknown"`. The factory sensor tracks the OpenAPI document's `info.version` (`1.0.0`). Hook payloads inside the VM report `cursor_version 1.0.0`, which is not reachable from outside the VM.

## Authentication and limits

- `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, where the key comes from `https://cursor.com/dashboard/api`. The provider reads `CURSOR_API_KEY`, and otherwise `cursor_api_key` under `[providers]` in `specstory.toml`.
- The documented limit is 20 requests per minute. The OpenAPI document promises `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` headers on `429`, but no rate-limit headers appeared on successful responses. The client spaces every request 3 s apart across the whole process and retries `429` and `5xx` responses, honouring `Retry-After` when it is present.
- Accounts on Privacy Mode (Legacy) get `400 validation_error` "Cloud agent is not supported in Privacy Mode (Legacy)" from every agent call.

## Endpoints read

| Call | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/me` | `{apiKeyName, userId, createdAt, userEmail, userFirstName, userLastName}`. Check reports `apiKeyName` only |
| `GET /v1/agents?limit=100&cursor=` | `{items:[agent], nextCursor?}`, newest first. `agent` = `{id: "bc-<uuid>", name, status: ACTIVE\|IDLE\|ARCHIVED, env, repos:[{url}], workOnCurrentBranch, autoCreatePR?, openAsCursorGithubApp, skipReviewerRequest, url, createdAt, updatedAt, latestRunId}` |
| `GET /v1/agents/{id}` | one `agent` |
| `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs` | `{items:[run]}`, newest first. `run` = `{id: "run-<uuid>", agentId, status: CREATING\|RUNNING\|FINISHED\|ERROR\|CANCELLED\|EXPIRED, createdAt, updatedAt, durationMs?, git:{branches:[{repoUrl, branch, prUrl?}]}}`. The single-run GET adds `result` (the final text); the list omits it |
| `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}/stream` | SSE, described below. Returns `410 {"error":{"code":"stream_expired","message":"Run stream is no longer available"}}` once retention has passed |
| `GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation` | `{id, messages:[{id, type: user_message\|assistant_message, text}]}`, covering every run of the agent, text only, with no timestamps. Kept indefinitely |
| `GET /v1/agents/{id}/usage` | `{totalUsage:{inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheWriteTokens, cacheReadTokens, totalTokens}, cost:{rawCostCents, chargedCents}, runs:[{id, usageUuid, usage, cost}]}` |

`repos[].url` on v1 is `https://github.com/org/repo`, while `git.branches[].repoUrl` and v0 `source.repository` are `github.com/org/repo`. Both normalize to the same string as the project's origin.

## Run stream grammar

Each SSE block has an optional `id: <epochMillis>-<seq>`, an `event: <name>` and a `data: <json>` line. The id is the only timestamp in the stream. Ids are not unique: a `thinking` event and its `interaction_update` `thinking-delta` share one. The stream is retained for `x-cursor-stream-retention-seconds: 86400` after a run ends. A finished run replays in full from the start, and the replay matches the live capture block for block, except that the opening `status` says `FINISHED` and live-only `heartbeat` events are absent.

| Event | Data | Rendering |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `{runId, status}` (no id) | none; the first and last block of a stream |
| `heartbeat` | `{}` (no id) | none; sent on a quiet live stream |
| `interaction_update` `user-message-appended` | `{userMessage:{type, session_id, text}}` | the user prompt, which is the only place the stream records it |
| `interaction_update` `token-delta`, `text-delta`, `thinking-delta` | deltas | none; these duplicate the typed events |
| `interaction_update` `step-started`, `step-completed`, `thinking-completed`, `tool-call-started`, `tool-call-completed`, `tool-requests-listed`, `partial-tool-call`, `turn-ended` | lifecycle | none |
| `thinking` | `{text}` delta | consecutive deltas concatenate into one thinking part |
| `assistant` | `{text}` delta | consecutive deltas concatenate into one text part |
| `tool_call` | `{callId, name, status: running\|completed, args?, result?}` | one tool message per `callId`, placed at its first event |
| `result` | `{runId, status, text, durationMs, git}` | its time ends the exchange; `text` repeats the final assistant text and is not rendered |
| `done` | `{}` | marks the end of the stream; a mirrored capture ending in `done` is whole |

A `tool_call` arrives several times per call. A `running` event may have no `args` yet while they stream in. The last event's fields win. A `running` event can carry a provisional `result: {error: {error: "Invalid arguments"}}` with `args: {toolCallId: "unknown-tool-call-id"}`, which the completed event then replaces, so results are taken only from non-`running` events.

Result shapes:

- Success: `{success: {...}}`.
- Tool failure: `{error: {error: "..."}}` (`delete_file`, `grep_search`, `web_fetch`, which also adds `url`) or `{error: {errorMessage: "..."}}` (`read_file`).
- A shell command that exits non-zero: `{failure: {command, exitCode, stderr, interleavedOutput, executionTime}, isBackground}`.

The provider removes the plumbing keys `toolCallId`, `conversationId` and `requestId` from inputs. Every tool path sits under the VM checkout `/workspace`. Paths are rendered relative to it, and path hints are rewritten onto the local project before they are made relative.

## Tools

The names recorded in `tool_call.name` differ from the names the model sees. `examples/tools.txt` holds both lists and the mapping between them.

| Name | Type | Input rendered | Result rendered |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run_terminal_cmd` | shell | `command` in a bash fence, plus `workingDirectory` when it is not `/workspace`. The summary uses `description` | `interleavedOutput` (or `stdout` + `stderr`) in a text fence. `failure` adds `Exit code`, and `isBackground` adds a note |
| `read_file` | read | `path` in the summary | `content` fenced by file extension, with a line range when partial |
| `edit_file` | write | the result's `diffString` as a diff, or `streamContent` while the call is still streaming | none (the diff is the body) |
| `delete_file` | write | `path` | `prevContent` as removed lines |
| `file_search` | search | `globPattern` in the summary, plus `targetDirectory` | file list |
| `grep_search` | search | `pattern` in the summary, plus `path` and flags | `file:line: content` lines from `workspaceResults` |
| `web_search` | search | `searchTerm` | each reference's `chunk`, which is already a markdown link list plus a synthesis |
| `web_fetch` | read | `url` | `markdown` in a markdown fence |
| `todo_write` | task | `todos[]` as a checklist (`TODO_STATUS_*` mapped) | none |
| `mcp` | generic | `serverIdentifier`, `toolName`; other arguments as JSON | `content[].text.text`; `structuredContent` repeats it and is omitted |
| `get_mcp_tools` | generic | `server`, `toolName` | `content` (a JSON string), plus `outputFilePath` |
| `await` | generic | `blockUntilMs` | `complete.runtimeMs` |
| `generate_image` | generic | `description`, `aspectRatio`, `filePath` | saved `filePath` |
| `write_canvas` / `read_canvas` | generic | `title` and `contents` / `canvasId` | link to the canvas `url`, plus `source` |
| `pr_management` | generic | seen once in the research spike, but not captured; rendered generically | generic |

Any other name renders as JSON with type `unknown`.

## Session model

- One agent is one session. The id is `bc-…`, `CreatedAt` is `agent.createdAt`, `UpdatedAt` is `agent.updatedAt`, and the slug comes from the first user prompt. `Name` is `agent.name`, which Cursor derives from the prompt when the launcher gives none.
- One run is one exchange, in `createdAt` order, and `ExchangeID` is the run id. `StartTime` is the first event id, and `EndTime` is the `result` event id. Metadata holds `runId`, `status`, `durationMs`, `branch`, `prUrl` and `agentUrl`.
- `Model` is empty because the API does not expose it. `Usage` is nil because usage is per run, not per message. Both stay in `RawData`.
- When a run's stream was never captured, or a finished run's capture is partial and the stream has expired, the exchange is built from the v0 conversation instead. That fallback is text only, and the exchange is marked `"source": "v0-conversation"`. Messages with ids `turn-N:…` belong to run index N; the first user message has a bare UUID id and belongs to turn 0. The user message takes the run's `createdAt` as its time, and agent messages have none.
- `WorkspaceRoot` is the caller's project path. `GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd` is empty: the API records a repository and never a directory, so reindex attributes these sessions to the `unknown` project.

## The mirror (write lifecycle)

The mirror defaults to `<project>/.specstory/cursorcloud/`. The `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` setting or `--user-data-dir cursorcloud:<path>` relocates it. A project-local mirror gets a `.gitignore` of `*`, because it holds unredacted raw transcripts.

```text
agents/<agentId>/agent.json                  agent object (written last in a refresh)
agents/<agentId>/conversation.json           v0 conversation
agents/<agentId>/usage.json                  usage
agents/<agentId>/runs/<runId>.json           run object from the run list
agents/<agentId>/runs/<runId>.events.jsonl   one {"id","event","data"} object per SSE block
```

- Every write is atomic (a temporary file, then a rename), and a file whose bytes are unchanged is not rewritten, so a sync that finds nothing new leaves every byte and mtime as it was.
- Runs, conversation and usage are re-fetched only when `agent.updatedAt` differs from the mirrored `agent.json`.
- A finished run whose events are missing or partial is replayed while it is within 24 h of its `updatedAt`. A `410` leaves the partial capture in place. A whole capture is never fetched again.
- `sync` never attaches to an unfinished run, because reading its stream blocks until the run ends. `watch` attaches live, appends events, and rewrites the file atomically after each burst.
- An agent directory without `agent.json` is not an agent yet. Readers skip it.

## Resume

Same-agent resume (`specstory resume` of a cloud session into `cursorcloud`) opens `https://cursor.com/agents/<id>`, where a follow-up run can be started, and then watches. Resuming another agent's session into `cursorcloud` is unsupported: the only way to create a cloud agent conversation is to launch a new paid run, so `ReconstructSession` returns `spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported`. Resuming a cloud session into a local agent works through the shared `SessionData` flattening.

### Notes on IDEs

With a specific session UUID:

```zsh
specstory sync -s <session-uuid>
```

### Non-default IDE install locations (`--user-data-dir`)

The `sync`, `check`, `list` and `watch` commands accept a repeatable `--user-data-dir` flag that points an IDE provider at a non-default install location — useful for portable installs and for reading a Windows-side install from WSL. It takes a `provider_id:path` pair where the path is the IDE's user-data-dir itself (the parent of the `User` directory), the same value the IDE's own `--user-data-dir` argument takes:

```zsh
specstory sync --user-data-dir cursoride:/opt/cursor/data --user-data-dir copilotide:/opt/vscode/data
```

Supported provider IDs are `cursoride`, `copilotide`, `copilotide-insiders`, `copilotide-vscodium` and `copilotide-vscodium-insiders`. If the override path doesn't exist, SpecStory warns and falls back to the standard location for your OS.

The `cursorcloud` provider reads them from the [Cloud Agents API](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints) with your Cursor API key (create one at https://cursor.com/dashboard/api, then set `CURSOR_API_KEY` or `cursor_api_key` under `[providers]`). Agents are matched to the current project by repository: an agent belongs to the project when one of its repositories is the project's git `origin`. The provider keeps a local mirror of what it has read in `.specstory/cursorcloud/` (it writes its own `.gitignore` there, because the mirror holds unredacted transcripts); `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` or `--user-data-dir cursorcloud:<path>` moves it. A finished run's full transcript, including tool calls and output, is available from the API for 24 hours; after that only its text remains, so sync at least daily or keep `specstory watch` running. `specstory run cursorcloud` opens https://cursor.com/agents in your browser and then watches until interrupted with `ctrl-c`. Resuming another agent's session into a cloud agent is not supported, because that would launch a new paid run; cloud sessions can be resumed into local agents.

### Notes on IDEs
""")

## How It Works
```
AI Coding Tools              Local First                  Cloud Platform
─────────────────           ─────────────                ─────────────────
                                                          (Login Required)
Cursor IDE         ┐
Copilot IDE        │
Claude Code CLI    │
Cursor CLI         │
Codex CLI          ├──────►  .specstory/history/  ──────►  cloud.specstory.com
Droid CLI          │          (Auto-Saved Locally)        (Search, Ask & Share)
DeepSeek TUI       │
Antigravity CLI    │
Grok Build         │
Muse Code          │
OpenCode           │
Pi                 │
Qwen Code          ┘
```

## Workflow

1. **Capture** - SpecStory CLI and IDE extensions save every AI interaction locally to `.specstory/history/`
2. **Sync (Optional)** - Sync your local sessions to SpecStory Cloud for safekeeping and team sharing
3. **Search** - Find conversations across all projects locally, or across multiple computers and team members in SpecStory Cloud
4. **Chat (Optional)** - Ask questions across your sessions in SpecStory Cloud to revisit decisions, understand past work, and find solutions
5. **Share** - Export and share specific solutions with your team
6. **Resume** - Resume sessions locally between different agents, and between multiple computers and team members with SpecStory Cloud
7. **Process** - Run [`/lore`](./lore) to mine your history into reusable, evidence-backed agent skills

## Supported Development Tools

SpecStory integrates seamlessly with your favorite AI coding tools, automatically saving all conversations locally to `.specstory/history/` in your project. **Everything is local-first** - your data stays on your machine unless you choose to sync to SpecStory Cloud.

### Terminal Coding Agents

**One installation works with all terminal coding agents** - Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Codex, Droid, DeepSeek, Antigravity CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code, and Pi:

```bash
# Check which agents are installed
specstory check

# Launch your preferred agent with session auto-save
specstory run claude       # Launch Claude Code
specstory run cursor       # Launch Cursor CLI
specstory run codex        # Launch Codex CLI
specstory run droid        # Launch Droid CLI
specstory run deepseek     # Launch DeepSeek TUI
specstory run antigravity  # Launch Antigravity CLI
specstory run grok         # Launch Grok Build
specstory run muse         # Launch Muse Code
specstory run opencode     # Launch OpenCode
specstory run qwen         # Launch Qwen Code
specstory run pi           # Launch Pi
specstory run              # Launch the default agent (Claude Code)

# Render all prior agent coding sessions in the project as markdown
specstory sync
```

All sessions automatically save to `.specstory/history/` in your current project.

> [!TIP]
> The SpecStory CLI acts as a wrapper that enhances any of these terminal agents with automatic session saving. You only need the respective agent installed (e.g., Claude Code) for SpecStory to work with it.

Learn much more about the [SpecStory CLI](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/tree/dev/specstory-cli).

## SpecStory Cloud ☁️

[**SpecStory Cloud**](https://cloud.specstory.com) transforms your local AI conversations into a powerful, centralized knowledge system.

### The Problem We Solve
- **Lost Context**: Critical decisions and solutions scattered across machines and projects
- **No Global Search**: Finding that perfect solution from last month is impossible
- **Fragile Sharing**: Passing around Markdown files doesn't scale

### The Solution
SpecStory Cloud creates your personal AI coding knowledge base:
- 🎯 **Explicit Opt-In**: Nothing syncs to SpecStory Cloud without an optional sign-up and login first
- 🔍 **Search Everywhere**: Full-text search across all your projects from all your computers.
- 💬 **Chat with Your History**: Ask questions across your sessions to revisit decisions, understand past work, and find solutions.
- 📚 **Organized by Project**: Automatic categorization by repository and time

# Specstory CLI Changelog

## v2.15.1 2026-09-24

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Your answers to Codex CLI's `request_user_input` questions are now included in saved markdown. Previously the question and options were saved, but the selected option and any note were dropped, leaving an empty result. Each question is now shown with its options and your answer underneath, and questions you cancelled are marked as unanswered. Thanks to [daviddwlee84](https://github.com/daviddwlee84) for the detailed report and reproduction in [issue 333](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/333).
- For Codex tools that SpecStory doesn't have a dedicated format for, the tool's arguments are now also shown as JSON. Previously they were lost whenever the tool also returned output.
- On Windows, `specstory run` and `specstory watch` no longer stop saving sessions partway through. Occasionally, when the agent created new session files while SpecStory was starting to watch a new directory, the file watcher could hang: no error was shown, and nothing more was saved to markdown or SpecStory Cloud until SpecStory was restarted. This could affect every supported agent.

## v2.15.0 2026-09-23

### 📢 Announcements

- The SpecStory CLI now supports [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) (i.e. `opencode`), the open source terminal coding agent, for sessions created from OpenCode version `2.0.14` or higher. Sessions from earlier versions may work, but are not officially supported. This provides the same support for saving to local markdown files and to the SpecStory Cloud as for [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/docs/api/claude-code), [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/docs/cli), [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/), Factory's [Droid CLI](https://factory.ai/product/cli), [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/product), Google's [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/), [DeepSeek TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI), [VS Code Copilot](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/copilot), [Muse Code](https://developer.meta.com/ai/products/muse-code/), [Pi](https://pi.dev), [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) and [Grok Build](https://x.ai/cli).
- OpenCode is a cross-provider `specstory resume` target: you can resume any agent's session into OpenCode, and resume an OpenCode session into another agent. OpenCode's free Zen models decline to continue a conversation that was not produced through Zen, so a resumed session needs another configured model to continue. Thanks to [marton78](https://github.com/marton78) for the original OpenCode provider contribution in [PR 156](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/156).

### ✏️ Markdown Enhancements

- Grok Build's image, video, workflow, scheduler, and feedback tools now render as readable fields in saved markdown, with prompts and workflow scripts in code blocks, instead of as raw JSON.
- Grok Build's `search_tool` now lists each discovered tool's parameters (type, whether required, and description) instead of its full JSON schema. A single tool search can return hundreds of tools, so saved sessions that search connected integrations are now much shorter.
- Grok Build shell commands, monitors, background-task lookups, images, workflows, scheduled tasks, and feedback drafts now show their command, prompt, name, or ID in the collapsed tool header, so a session can be scanned without expanding each tool.
- Grok Build tool results no longer include Grok's notices about unrelated background tasks, or the wrapper tags around `grep` results. A background shell command's task ID, status, and output file now show as labeled fields.
- Grok Build `use_tool` results that are JSON are now shown in a JSON code block, and several tool fields now have consistently capitalized labels (e.g. `URL`, `Query`, `Description`).

## v2.14.1 2026-09-22

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Claude Code sessions are now found when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set. Claude Code uses this variable to run separate profiles (for example, a personal and a work account), each storing its sessions in `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`, but SpecStory only read `~/.claude/projects`. As a result, `specstory sync` reported the sessions as not found, and `specstory run` and `specstory watch` silently saved nothing. SpecStory now reads from the same place Claude Code writes to, so `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.claude-work" specstory run claude` saves that profile's sessions without symlinking its `projects` directory into `~/.claude`. Thanks to [simkimsia](https://github.com/simkimsia) for the detailed report in [issue 325](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/325).
- Codex CLI tool output from code mode `exec` calls is now included in saved markdown and SpecStory Cloud sessions. Previously this output was silently dropped because Codex writes it as a list of content parts rather than as text. Images in tool output are noted with an `[image]` marker rather than embedded.
- Long Codex CLI tool output is now truncated after 5000 characters instead of 5000 bytes, so the cut no longer splits multi-byte characters (e.g. Chinese text or emoji) and leaves saved markdown as invalid UTF-8. Thanks to [daviddwlee84](https://github.com/daviddwlee84) for reporting the same problem with Codex custom-tool inputs in [issue 311](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/311), which was resolved in v2.13.0.
- Session names derived from a long first prompt are now shortened to 100 characters instead of 100 bytes. Prompts written without spaces, such as Chinese, no longer end in `��` replacement characters in `specstory list`, `specstory resume`, and SpecStory Cloud session titles.

## v2.14.0 2026-09-22

### 📢 Announcements

- The SpecStory CLI now supports [Grok Build](https://x.ai/cli) (i.e. `grok`, `agent`), SpaceXAI's terminal coding agent, for sessions created from Grok Build version `1.0.34` or higher. Sessions from earlier versions may work, but are not officially supported. This provides the same support for saving to local markdown files and to the SpecStory Cloud as for [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/docs/api/claude-code), [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/docs/cli), [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/), Factory's [Droid CLI](https://factory.ai/product/cli), [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/product), Google's [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/), [DeepSeek TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI), [VS Code Copilot](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/copilot), [Muse Code](https://developer.meta.com/ai/products/muse-code/), [Pi](https://pi.dev) and [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code).
- Grok is a cross-provider `specstory resume` target: you can resume any agent's session into Grok, and resume a Grok session into another agent.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Bare `specstory run` launches Claude Code as documented, rather than choosing the first provider alphabetically. The help text and configured command now use the same default.
- Muse Code sessions containing a single JSONL line larger than the 64MB limit now render with that line skipped, instead of failing to render the whole session.

## v2.13.0 2026-09-17

### ⚙️ Improvements

- `specstory check` now treats missing optional agents as informational instead of showing a failed check for each agent you haven't installed. Permission problems, broken installations, and unreadable IDE storage still appear as errors, as does a missing custom command supplied with `-c`. Exit codes are unchanged.
- Pi transcripts now include edit diffs, read ranges, search options, and clearer PowerShell tool output. Narration and tool calls retain their original order, and unfamiliar tool fields are preserved instead of silently omitted.
- `specstory skills` now recognizes Pi as an installation target, using `.pi/skills` for project skills and `~/.pi/agent/skills` for global skills.
- Claude Code live session saving (`specstory run` or `specstory watch`) now defers file writes (transcript, statistics, and debug writes) while a Bash or PowerShell tool call is in progress, reducing cases where Claude Code 2.1.269+ diff sweep incorrectly shows SpecStory's files as edits made by those commands. Deferred updates are flushed on shutdown. `specstory sync` and final exports after Claude exits still write immediately, and a five-minute fallback prioritizes saving SpecStory history in case of a hung tool call, so very long commands that eventually do finish may still show these edits as originating with the tool.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Improved saving when a coding agent exits: pending session updates finish in order, and final writes are picked up before `specstory run` returns. This fixes shutdown paths that could lose the last update or let an older save overwrite a newer one, including when an agent exits with an error. The agent's exit status is preserved.
- Selecting a session to resume now overrides conflicting resume flags in custom commands for Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Droid, Gemini, Antigravity, and DeepSeek TUI. Previously a configured session ID could take precedence over the session you selected.
- Cursor CLI live saving now picks up changes to existing sessions resumed outside SpecStory, rather than ignoring sessions that were already present when watching started. Reading a newly created session before its first message has been written no longer causes a crash.

# Manual row: `watch cursorcloud`, then a new run launched through the API appears live.

  # The run is done when the markdown contains the follow-up's reply after the third prompt.
  if grep -q "live-watch test" "$md" && [ "$(grep -c 'Tool use: \*\*run_terminal_cmd' "$md")" -ge 5 ] && grep -q "FINISHED\|^---" "$md"; then
    st=$(curl -sS --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $CURSOR_API_KEY" "https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents/$AGENT/runs" | python3 -I -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["items"][0]["status"])')
    echo "latest run status $st" >> "$OUT/timeline"
    [ "$st" = "FINISHED" ] && break
  fi
done
sleep 15
kill -INT $WPID
wait $WPID
echo "watch exit=$?" >> "$OUT/timeline"
shasum "$md" > "$OUT/md-after.sha"
cp "$md" "$OUT/history-after.md"

cat >> docs/PROVIDER-GUIDE-FEEDBACK.md <<'EOF'

## 14. "Rendering": failure is not always an error branch (impl)

"A failed call renders the agent's error text; the error branch takes priority over the success formatter for every tool" assumes one failure shape. Cursor Cloud records three: `result.error.error` (delete, grep, web fetch), `result.error.errorMessage` (read), and, for a shell command that exits non-zero, a separate `result.failure` branch carrying `exitCode` and `stderr` rather than an error. A renderer that only checks the error branch shows a failed command as a success with no output.

Proposed: "Capture at least one deliberately failed call per tool family and render every failure shape you observe, including non-zero shell exits recorded outside the error branch. Show the exit code with the output."

## 15. "Parsing": provisional results on in-progress records (impl)

The guide says results are paired by native correlation fields and does not cover a record that is updated several times. Cursor Cloud emits several `tool_call` events per call id. A `running` event can carry a placeholder `{"error":{"error":"Invalid arguments"}}` while arguments are still streaming, and the completed event later replaces it. A naive "last field wins" merge is correct only when the call completes. For a call interrupted mid-stream it would render a fake error.

Proposed: "When a call is re-serialized on every state update, merge field by field, and take results only from records the native format marks as final. Test an interrupted call."

## 16. "The watcher": mapping the acceptance cases onto a poller (impl)

The acceptance cases held up, but each needed a translation that the guide could state once:

| Guide case | Poller equivalent used |
| --- | --- |
| File written before startup, unchanged | Agent listed at the baseline poll, `updatedAt` unchanged afterwards |
| File changes while the baseline is established | The baseline records the `updatedAt` it listed; a change during the baseline's own fetches is seen as an advance by the next poll |
| Directory appears after startup with old mtimes | Agent first listed after the baseline, whatever its `createdAt` |
| Pre-existing directory discovered late in the initial scan | Agent on a later page of the baseline listing |
| Shutdown with nothing pending | Stop joins every poll and stream goroutine; an undelivered burst is drained, nothing else is emitted |

Two additions only a remote store needs: live events replayed on attach must not count as new activity (the provider counts only events stamped after the watcher started), and a resumed stream (`Last-Event-ID`) may repeat events, because SSE ids are not unique in this API. Proposed: add the table above under "For a remote store" next to entry 3.

## 17. Wiring tests assume every `[providers]` key is a command (impl)

`TestProvidersConfigIsFullyWired` derives a provider id from every `ProvidersConfig` field by stripping `_cmd`. The two new settings, `cursor_api_key` and `cursorcloud_mirror_dir`, made it fail. The test now skips non-`_cmd` keys that are listed in an explicit `nonCommandProviderSettings` allowlist, so a new key is still a deliberate choice. The settings reach the provider through `cmd.ApplyProviderSettings`, called from `main.go` right after the config loads.

Proposed: in "Wiring outside the package", add "A provider setting that is not a launch command goes in `ProvidersConfig`, in the template, in `nonCommandProviderSettings` in the config test, and in `cmd.ApplyProviderSettings`, which hands it to a package-level setter."

## 18. `check <id> -c` for a provider with no binary (impl)

The manual table says "`-c` with a bad path fails with guidance naming that path". For `cursorcloud`, `-c`/`cursorcloud_cmd` is the URL opener that `run` uses. `Check` therefore resolves a custom opener with `spi.LookPathForCheck` and fails as `not_found` naming it, then probes the API. The guide should say what `-c` means for a provider with no binary.

## 19. Global enumeration with a per-project store (impl)

`ListAllAgentChatSessions` takes no project and assumes one global native store. The plan puts the mirror inside each project by default, so reindex sees only the mirror under the current working directory, plus any shared `cursorcloud_mirror_dir`, unless the user configures a shared location. This is a consequence of choosing a project-local store and is documented in the format doc. The guide could note that a provider whose store is per-project can enumerate only the store it can locate.

## 20. Path hints from a remote workspace (impl)

The guide covers recorded paths from another OS but not from another machine with a different root. Every Cursor Cloud tool path is under the VM checkout `/workspace`. The provider rewrites that prefix onto the local project before `spi.NormalizePath`, so hints become project-relative like every other provider's, and it renders paths relative to `/workspace`. Proposed: "If the agent runs in a remote checkout with a fixed root, map that root onto the local project for hints and rendering. Never treat it as a local path."

## 21. Per-save feedback during `run` is keyed to IDE ids (impl)

"IDE providers only: the per-save line during `run` … keyed to the registry id in `main.go`". The real criterion is "the provider does not own the terminal", which also covers a hosted agent followed from a browser. `cursorcloud` was added to that branch. Proposed: reword to "Providers whose `run` does not hand the terminal to an agent (IDEs, hosted agents)".

## 22. `tools.txt` placement (impl)

The sweep test reads section 1 of `examples/tools.txt` so that the expected-type table cannot drift from the inventory. The guide says examples are review artifacts and that `testdata/` holds what tests consume. A test-consumed `tools.txt` therefore arguably belongs in `testdata/`, but every other provider keeps it with the review artifacts. Proposed: state where a test-consumed inventory lives.

## 23. Mirror and git (impl, resolves 13 provisionally)

The implementation writes `.specstory/cursorcloud/.gitignore` containing `*` when the mirror is project-local. The mirror holds unredacted transcripts, and cloud tool output can include environment dumps. A shared mirror location gets no `.gitignore`. This is a reversible default chosen to avoid committing secrets; Sean's decision on entry 13 can change it to documentation-only.

## 24. Lint tooling version (impl)

The installed `golangci-lint` 2.13.2 cannot read Go 1.27.2 export data ("export data version 5 is greater than maximum supported version 4"), even when rebuilt with the local toolchain. v2.14.0 works and reports 0 issues. Proposed: the guide's lint step could pin a minimum `golangci-lint` version alongside the Go version in `go.mod`.

```text
package cmd

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"regexp"
	"strings"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/cloud"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/sessionindex"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/utils"
)

// Direct session addressing for `specstory resume --session <uri>`.
//
// A session can be chosen interactively in the TUI, or now directly via a session URI. The
// driving use case is the Cloud web app's Resume button, which copies a paste-able command
// carrying exactly the two IDs the cloud API needs (project_id + native session id). The URI
// resolves to the same session identity the picker would produce — including the
// local-preferred guard: a session that also exists locally resumes in place — and feeds the
// identical resumePlan → launchResume machinery, so there is no parallel resume implementation.

// sessionURI is a parsed --session argument: a project id + native session id, plus (for
// pasted web permalinks only) the origin the link points at so resolveSessionURI can refuse
// a host that differs from the configured cloud.
// projectID is empty for the bare-UUID form (resolved local-first, then cloud-discovered).
type sessionURI struct {
	projectID string // "" for a bare session UUID
	sessionID string // normalized (lowercase) native session uuid
	host      string // permalink origin (scheme://host[:port]); "" for specstory:// and bare UUID
}

// Project ids are the CLI-minted truncated-SHA form: xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx (16 hex chars,
// createHash in pkg/utils/project_identity.go). Session ids are provider-generated UUIDs:
// xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx. Both are matched case-insensitively.
var (
	projectIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}$`)
	sessionIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`)
)

// parseSessionURI parses the three accepted --session forms:
//
//  1. specstory://projects/{projectID}/sessions/{sessionID} — the canonical, host-free form the
//     web app copies. url.Parse puts "projects" in Host for a custom scheme, so host+path
//     are rejoined before matching.
//  2. https://{host}/projects/{projectID}/sessions/{sessionID} — a pasted browser permalink.
//     Trailing slashes are tolerated and any path segments after the session id (e.g.
//     /chats/{chatId}) are ignored, so any session-page URL pastes cleanly.
//  3. {sessionUUID} — bare session id shorthand; resolves local-first then cloud.
//
// ID shapes are validated up front for early, clear errors.
func parseSessionURI(raw string) (sessionURI, error) {
	raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
	if raw == "" {
		return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: "--session requires a session URI or UUID"}
	}

	// A bare UUID has no scheme delimiter. Detect it before url.Parse (which would treat it as a
	// path and lose nothing, but validating the shape here gives the clearest error).
	if !strings.Contains(raw, "://") && sessionIDRe.MatchString(raw) {
		return sessionURI{sessionID: strings.ToLower(raw)}, nil
	}

	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
	if err != nil {
		return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf("invalid session URI %q: %v", raw, err)}
	}

	switch u.Scheme {
	case "specstory":
		// For a custom (non-special) scheme, url.Parse lands "projects" in Host and the rest in
		// Path. Rejoin them so the /projects/{id}/sessions/{id} grammar matches the permalink form.
		segs := pathSegments(u.Host + u.Path)
		uri, ok := matchSessionPath(segs)
		if !ok {
			return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
				"invalid specstory: URI %q — expected specstory://projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}", raw)}
		}
		return uri, nil
	case "http", "https":
		segs := pathSegments(u.Path)
		uri, ok := matchSessionPath(segs)
		if !ok {
			return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
				"invalid session URL %q — expected /projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}", raw)}
		}
		uri.host = u.Scheme + "://" + u.Host
		return uri, nil
	default:
		// A bare non-UUID string (or any other scheme): report a shape error rather than silently
		// treating garbage as a session id.
		return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
			"unsupported session URI %q — use specstory://projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}, a cloud permalink, or a session UUID", raw)}
	}
}

// matchSessionPath validates the /projects/{pid}/sessions/{sid}[/…] segment grammar and returns
// the parsed URI (shapes validated, ids lowercased) or ok=false.
func matchSessionPath(segs []string) (sessionURI, bool) {
	if len(segs) < 4 || segs[0] != "projects" || segs[2] != "sessions" {
		return sessionURI{}, false
	}
	pid, sid := segs[1], segs[3]
	if !projectIDRe.MatchString(pid) {
		return sessionURI{}, false
	}
	if !sessionIDRe.MatchString(sid) {
		return sessionURI{}, false
	}
	return sessionURI{
		projectID: strings.ToLower(pid),
		sessionID: strings.ToLower(sid),
	}, true
}

// pathSegments splits a URL path (or rejoined host+path) on "/" and drops empty segments, so
// trailing slashes ("/…/sessions/sid/") and any "/chats/{id}" tail collapse to the same token

// buildSession turns one enumeration ref into a fully-built index row. Every session
// yields a row from its metadata; the body + turn counts + last-activity time are
// ENRICHED via a full parse only when the originating cwd lets us re-locate the
// session (so Cursor, whose cwd is unknown for now, lands metadata-only). Nothing is
// dropped.
func buildSession(item reindexItem, cache *projectIDCache, indexedAt string) sessionindex.Session {
	ref := item.ref
	projectID, projectName := cache.resolve(ref.OriginCwd)

	sess := sessionindex.Session{
		ProjectID:    projectID,
		ProjectName:  projectName,
		Agent:        item.agent,
		SessionID:    ref.SessionID,
		CreatedAt:    ref.CreatedAt,
		UpdatedAt:    ref.CreatedAt, // default; overwritten by last-turn timestamp below
		Slug:         ref.Slug,
		Name:         ref.Name,
		NativePath:   ref.NativePath,
		OriginCwd:    ref.OriginCwd,
		Size:         item.size, // captured during the freshness check (no re-stat)
		Mtime:        item.mtime,
		IndexVersion: reindexVersion,
		IndexedAt:    indexedAt,
		IsNew:        item.isNew,
	}

	if ref.OriginCwd == "" {
		return sess // cannot re-locate without a cwd → metadata-only
	}
	full, err := parseFullSession(item.prov, ref)
	if err != nil || full == nil || full.SessionData == nil {
		slog.Debug("reindex: full parse unavailable, indexing metadata only",
			"agent", item.agent, "session", ref.SessionID, "error", err)
		return sess
	}

	data := full.SessionData
	sess.Body = flattenBody(data)
	sess.UserTurns, sess.TotalTurns = countTurns(data)
	if ts := lastTimestamp(data); ts != "" {
		sess.UpdatedAt = ts
	}
	return sess
}

// parseFullSession reads a session's full data for indexing. It prefers a provider's
// path-keyed parse (spi.PathSessionReader) using the ref's already-known NativePath, which
// avoids the provider's by-id discovery search — for Codex that search walks the entire
// ~/.codex/sessions tree, so this is the difference between an O(N) and an O(N²) reindex.
// Providers without the capability (or refs lacking a NativePath) fall back to the by-id
// lookup. Parsing the known NativePath is also more consistent: a row's freshness
// fingerprint is stat'd from NativePath (unless the provider supplied its own), so the
// body now comes from that same file.
func parseFullSession(prov spi.Provider, ref spi.GlobalSessionRef) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	if pr, ok := prov.(spi.PathSessionReader); ok && ref.NativePath != "" {
		return pr.GetAgentChatSessionByPath(ref.NativePath, ref.OriginCwd, false)
	}
	return prov.GetAgentChatSession(ref.OriginCwd, ref.SessionID, false)
}

// drainToStore writes parsed sessions to the index in batched transactions.
func drainToStore(store *sessionindex.Store, ch <-chan sessionindex.Session) error {
	batch := make([]sessionindex.Session, 0, reindexWriteBatch)
	flush := func() error {
		if err := store.UpsertBatch(batch); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		batch = batch[:0]
		return nil
	}
	for sess := range ch {
		batch = append(batch, sess)
		if len(batch) >= reindexWriteBatch {
			if err := flush(); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
	}
	return flush()
}

// ---- session field derivation ----

// flattenBody renders SessionData to plain user/agent text for full-text indexing,
// reusing the reconstruction flattener (synthetic noise already stripped). No
// migration note is prepended — this is index content, not a resumed transcript.
func flattenBody(data *schema.SessionData) string {
	turns := spi.FlattenSessionData(data, "")
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, t := range turns {
		if t.Text == "" {
			continue
		}
		if b.Len() > 0 {
			b.WriteString("\n\n")
		}
		b.WriteString(t.Text)
	}
	return b.String()
}
