## 25. Empty `OriginCwd` costs more than attribution (impl, extends 9)

Entry 9 expected cloud sessions to land in the `unknown` project. In practice the effect is larger. `reindex` (and the resume picker, which refreshes the index on start) only parses a session's body when `OriginCwd` is set. With it empty, every cloud session is indexed metadata-only: no searchable text, zero turns, `unknown` project. This also overwrites the complete rows that `sync`'s live indexer had just written (correct project id, origin cwd and full body). As a result, `search` and the picker's `/` search never find text from a cloud session, and the session's own project shows no cloud sessions after the next reindex. This was observed in the manual run: after `sync`, all five rows had bodies of 3–39 KB under the project's `git_id`; after `reindex`, all five had empty bodies under `unknown`.

Two fixes, for Sean to choose between:

- Provider-only (small): when the mirror is project-local, the project that holds it is known, and the provider has already checked that the project's origin matches the agent's repository. `ListAllAgentChatSessions` could set `OriginCwd` to that project root. This contradicts the plan's "OriginCwd stays empty" and the guide's strict reading of "originating working directory", so it was not done.
- SPI: `GlobalSessionRef.OriginRepoURL` (entry 9), plus reindex parsing bodies for refs that carry it.

## 26. `resume --session` accepts only UUID-shaped ids (impl)

`pkg/cmd/session_uri.go` validates session ids against a UUID pattern, so `specstory resume --session bc-<uuid>` is rejected, and so would be a cloud permalink for a cloud agent session. The picker path works. The guide does not say that session ids must be UUIDs, and `spi.AgentChatSession.SessionID` only says "often a UUID". Proposed: either state the UUID requirement in the guide (which `cursorcloud` cannot meet) or relax the `--session` pattern to the id shapes providers actually use.
EOF

The Cursor Cloud Agent provider is built and wired. The automated checks pass, and every row of the section 8 table was run against the real API except the search TUI. The real gap is `search`: text from cloud sessions is never searchable, because of the plan's empty-`OriginCwd` decision (details below). Nothing is committed.

## Checks

- **gofmt:** clean.
- **golangci-lint:** 0 issues, but only with v2.14.0. The Homebrew v2.13.2 can't read Go 1.27.2 build data and fails on files I didn't touch. I ran v2.14.0 via `go run`; `go.mod` is unchanged.
- **`go test ./...`:** all 30 packages pass. The new package also passed 5 runs with `-race`.
- **Windows build and vet:** both pass.
- **Factory sensor:** `factory/latest-version` prints `1.0.0` (the published API spec's version) under an isolated home, and both failure cases exit non-zero.

## Section 8 table

| Row | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `check cursorcloud`, with and without a key, and with a bad `-c` path | Pass. Shows the key name; missing key gives guidance; the bad path is named |
| `sync`, then a second `sync` | Pass. 5 agents gave 5 markdown files; the second sync changed no bytes or mtimes and took 2.8 s |
| `sync --debug-raw --log` | Pass. Debug files as the plan specifies, no schema warnings |
| `watch cursorcloud` plus a new run | Pass. Picked up on the next poll |
| `run cursorcloud -c echo` plus a slow run | Pass. Followed the run live: 5 saves during it, capture complete with no duplicates, clean exit |
| `list` and `reindex` | Pass. Slugs match the filenames; reindex counts 5 cloud sessions |
| `search` | **Not run.** `codex --version` hangs on this machine, which blocks the search TUI's startup. I checked the index directly instead |
| `resume claude` from a cloud session | Pass. Driven through tmux: migration note first, thinking and tools as text, and Claude answered questions about the history correctly |
| Resume into `cursorcloud` | Refused with a clear message |
| `sync -s` and `sync -s --print`; no-origin directory; symlink and space-plus-underscore paths | Pass. `--print` wrote no files; the no-origin directory prints guidance and exits 0 |

## What still needs your decision

- **Cloud session text is never searchable.** Because `OriginCwd` is empty (as planned), `reindex` stores cloud sessions with no text and the `unknown` project. It overwrites the complete rows `sync` just wrote. The resume picker reindexes on start, so the picker's search never finds cloud text either. A small provider-only fix exists (the project-local mirror knows its project), but it reverses a planned decision, so I left it. Feedback entry 25 has both options.
- **The mirror `.gitignore` (your open question 1).** I chose the safe default: the project-local mirror writes `.gitignore` with `*`, since it holds unredacted transcripts. It's easy to change.
- **`resume --session bc-…` is rejected.** That parser only accepts UUID-shaped ids; the picker works.
- **`run cursorcloud` opens the dashboard and watches (your open question 2).** Implemented as planned.

## Where the plan didn't match what the API does

- **Failure shapes.** Real failures appear in three forms: `error.error`, `error.errorMessage`, and a separate `result.failure` (with exit code and stderr) for a shell command that exits non-zero. All three render.
- **"Invalid arguments" errors.** The ones in the original fixture are placeholders on in-progress events that later succeed. They aren't real failures, so the renderer ignores them.
- **`heartbeat` events.** The live stream sends them and the plan didn't list them; they're handled.
- **Mirror bytes.** Saving events could rewrite `&&` as `\u0026\u0026`. I fixed that so the mirror keeps the stream's exact bytes.

## Paid runs and other changes

I made four paid cloud runs on `specstoryai/cloud-agent-test`: one new agent plus three follow-ups. The first two cost about 24¢ together; I didn't fetch the cost of the other two.

Outside the package:
- **Shared code:** the git-origin helpers moved into `pkg/spi/git_origin.go`, with `pkg/utils` calling them.
- **Wiring:** registry, config, `run` output and TUI color are updated.
- **Config test:** I changed `TestProvidersConfigIsFullyWired` so it allows the two new settings that aren't launch commands.
- **Docs:** both READMEs and the changelog are updated, and `CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md` and `examples/TOOL-AUDIT.md` are new. I added entries 14–26 to `docs/PROVIDER-GUIDE-FEEDBACK.md`; the guide itself is untouched.
- **Test repo:** the manual runs left a `.specstory/` directory in `~/Source/SpecStory/cloud-agent-test`.

// TestComputeProjectIDFromRemoteMatchesCheckout guards the contract hosted-agent
// sessions rely on: a session that names only its repository must land in the
// same project as a local clone of that repository, whichever URL form each uses.
func TestComputeProjectIDFromRemoteMatchesCheckout(t *testing.T) {
	repo := t.TempDir()
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(repo, ".git"), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cfg := "[remote \"origin\"]\n\turl = git@github.com:specstoryai/cloud-agent-test.git\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(repo, ".git", "config"), []byte(cfg), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	wantID, wantName, err := ComputeProjectID(repo)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, remote := range []string{
		"https://github.com/specstoryai/cloud-agent-test",
		"github.com/specstoryai/cloud-agent-test",
	} {
		id, name, err := ComputeProjectIDFromRemote(remote)
		if err != nil || id != wantID || name != wantName {
			t.Errorf("ComputeProjectIDFromRemote(%q) = (%q, %q, %v); want (%q, %q)", remote, id, name, err, wantID, wantName)
		}
	}
	if _, _, err := ComputeProjectIDFromRemote(" "); err == nil {
		t.Error("an empty remote URL must be an error")
	}
}
EOF

}

## The resume-from-another-directory question

**How a cloud session is found when you resume it.** Most agents' sessions are files on your disk. When you resume one, SpecStory reads that file directly. A Cursor Cloud Agent session has no file of its own. SpecStory keeps its copy in a mirror inside the project you synced from (`<project>/.specstory/cursorcloud/`), or asks the Cursor API for it.

To work out which project a cloud agent belongs to, the provider compares the agent's GitHub repository with the git `origin` of the directory it's asked about. That check stops one project's agent being saved into another project's history.

**When it works and when it doesn't.** When you resume, SpecStory tells the provider which directory the session came from. For a cloud session that directory is blank, because Cursor never records one, so the provider falls back to the directory you ran `specstory resume` from:

- **It works** when you run `resume` from inside a clone of the agent's repository, such as `~/Source/SpecStory/cloud-agent-test`. The picker opens on that project by default, and that's the path I tested.
- **It fails** when you run `specstory resume` from an unrelated project, press tab to browse all projects, and pick a cloud session from there. The current directory's `origin` doesn't match the agent's repository, so the provider reports "not found". If you have no clone of that repository on this machine, there's no directory where it would succeed.

**Your options:**
- **Leave it and document it.** Cloud sessions resume from a clone of their repository. It's simple and always safe, and it's the common case.
- **Fix it.** Doing that properly means a small shared-code change. Resume would pass the session's recorded repository (which reindex already stores) to the provider. The provider would then look the agent up by that repository instead of the current directory, and fetch it from the API if this machine's mirror doesn't have it.

Which would you like?

// agentIDByNameFromRegistry builds the agent display-name → provider-id map that cloud row
// conversion (cloudToSessions) needs to resolve a cloud session's metadata.agentName back to
// the provider id the resume/reconstruct path keys on. Mirrors the map newSessionTUI builds
// from the TUI's agentMeta set, but from the registry alone so non-TUI callers (--session)
// can build it without constructing a picker.
func agentIDByNameFromRegistry(registry *factory.Registry) map[string]string {
	out := make(map[string]string)
	for _, id := range registry.ListIDs() {
		prov, err := registry.Get(id)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		out[prov.Name()] = id
	}
	return out
}

// resumePlanFromSession builds a resumePlan for a directly-resolved session (the --session path
// with a preset agent), reusing the same selection-time guard and plan shape as the TUI tail.
// targetID is the preset agent; it must be a known, INSTALLED provider to resume into (mirroring
// selectResumeViaTUI's installed check, which the non-interactive path can't inherit).
func resumePlanFromSession(registry *factory.Registry, store *sessionindex.Store, s *sessionindex.Session, targetID string) (*resumePlan, error) {
	fromProv, err := registry.Get(s.Agent)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown source agent %q: %w", s.Agent, err)
	}
	toProv, err := registry.Get(targetID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
			"unknown agent %q. Valid agents: %s", targetID, registry.GetProviderList())}
	}
	if !toProv.Check("").Success {
		return nil, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
			"agent %q is not installed, so it can't be a resume target.", targetID)}
	}
	fromCloud, fromCwd := resumeSourceForSession(store, s)
	return &resumePlan{
		from:      fromProv,
		fromID:    s.Agent,
		sessionID: s.SessionID,
		fromCwd:   fromCwd,
		to:        toProv,
		toID:      targetID,
		fromCloud: fromCloud,
		projectID: s.ProjectID,
	}, nil
}

// resumeSourceForSession applies the selection-time guard: a cloud-badged row can be a session
// that is ALSO present locally (e.g. a cloud search hit that local FTS didn't match). When it is,
// prefer the local copy — an in-place resume is instant, works offline, and doesn't mint a fresh
// reconstructed session id — over the cloud fetch/reconstruct path. Returns the fromCloud flag and
// fromCwd for the resume plan. A soft-deleted local row does NOT count (GetSession filters it), so
// a session you deleted locally still resumes from the cloud. In browse this never fires — dedup
// already dropped any cloud row with a local twin — but cloud search can surface such a row.
func resumeSourceForSession(store *sessionindex.Store, s *sessionindex.Session) (fromCloud bool, fromCwd string) {
	fromCloud = s.IsCloud
	fromCwd = s.OriginCwd
	if s.IsCloud {
		if local, ok, err := store.GetSession(s.Agent, s.SessionID); err == nil && ok {
			fromCloud = false
			fromCwd = local.OriginCwd
		}
	}
	return fromCloud, fromCwd
}
